articles.title: Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel kill five people on Mexico’s Pacific coast
articles.summary:
Security forces use helicopters to rescue dozens of people as the two storms damage infrastructure and cause flash flooding

At least five people have died after Hurricane Simon and Tropical…

blocks.text: At least five people have died after Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel pummelled Mexico’s Pacific coast, causing flooding that downed trees and electricity poles, blocked roads and inundated homes.
Simon claimed the life of a 71-year-old man who died when a wall collapsed in Chilpancingo in the southern state of Guerrero, governor Evelyn Salgado said at a press conference.
The storm also damaged infrastructure and homes in the state’s coastal towns, including the major seaport of Acapulco, she said.

Tropical Storm Rachel is blamed for the deaths of four members of one family, including two children, whose bodies were found on the outskirts of the city of Ensenada in Baja California, the state’s prosecutor’s office reported.

Five more people remained missing, while security forces used helicopters to rescue 32 people, prosecutors said. Baja governor Marina del Pilar said officials were helping more than 50 people in temporary shelters.

blocks.caption: Hurricane Simon has flooded streets in towns along Mexico’s Pacific coast. Photograph: Christian Ruano/Reuters

blocks.text: Simon did not make landfall and, after weakening to category two on the five-point Saffir-Simpson scale, was moving away from the coast, authorities said. A rain alert remained in place.
The National Hurricane Center in Miami said heavy rainfall associated with Simon in west-central Mexico over the next few days might still produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides.

Officials warned waves of up to five metres high were still expected in some coastal areas. Flooding and landslides had already hit communities close to rivers and streams in the states of Michoacan and Colima.

blocks.caption: A man walks past a boarded-up business in Puerto Vallarta bearing the message ‘Simon, be brief, be peaceful’. Photograph: Christian Ruano/Reuters

blocks.text: The El Niño phenomenon, characterised by rising water temperatures in the Pacific, is fuelling a more intense hurricanes this season in the region.

Meteorologists say the 2026-27 El Niño, which causes global changes in winds and rainfall as well as erratic weather conditions, is certain to be the biggest ever recorded. Scientists now also think human-caused global heating is making El Niños more intense.
With Agence France-Presse and Associated Press

articles.title: Bedbug infestation forces Qantas to ground plane in Rome
articles.summary:
Aircraft taken out of operation after flight from Perth after the discovery of parasitic insects on board

Qantas has been forced to ground a plane in Rome after bedbugs were discovered on…

blocks.text: Qantas has been forced to ground a plane in Rome after bedbugs were discovered on the aircraft on its way from Perth.

The parasitic insects were found in the front of the economy section of the Boeing 787 Dreamliner as it made its way from Perth to Rome for the QF5 flight on 9 October, a source with knowledge of the incident confirmed on Tuesday.
Bed bugs are small insects that feed on the blood of some mammals, including humans, which can be hard to eradicate.

As first reported by the SMH, the aircraft had to be taken out of service for cleaning after its arrival in the Italian capital, resulting in the cancellation of the Qantas Rome to Perth service on 10 October.

A Qantas spokesperson said the flight was cancelled to allow its engineers and maintenance teams to carry out a deep clean of the aircraft after “an issue identified on a small number of economy seats”.
They said the airline wanted to “sincerely apologise” to customers for the disruption.

blocks.caption: The bed bugs were most likely brought onto the plane in someone’s luggage or on a passenger’s clothes. Photograph: Lamara Dalzous/Alamy

blocks.text: Affected passengers were given accommodation and rebooked on alternative flights within 48 hours of their original departure, Qantas said.
The airline said its aircraft cabins were cleaned regularly and to an extremely high standard and treated with disinfectant every 50 days as a standard precautionary cleaning measure.

Prof Michelle Power, a parasitologist at Macquarie University, said the bedbugs had “more than likely” been brought onto the plane in someone’s luggage or on a passenger’s clothes and then escaped into the cabin.

“They’re associated with travel. People may go to a hotel that’s infested and because they like dark spaces and are attracted to the smell of human clothes, they make their way into someone’s luggage.”
“They’re a flightless insect, without planes,” she said.

Power said bedbugs were not dangerous, even though their bites could be itchy and irritating, but they were very difficult to get rid of and could hide in bedsheets and crevices for a long time without needing to feed.

She said there were “two sides to bed bugs”: on the one hand, wealthier people who travelled a lot got them and subsequently moved them around, whereas people already experiencing health inequities may not be able to afford pesticides or potentially heat water to the 55C required to kill them.

articles.title: 27 Chinese vessels monitored in West Philippine Sea in past 6 days
articles.summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Tuesday said that there were at least 27 Chinese vessels monitored across several West Philippine Sea (WPS) features from October 6 to October 12.

blocks.text: Published October 13, 2026 12:11pm
At least 27 Chinese vessels were monitored in parts of the West Philippine Sea (WPS) from October 6 to October 12, according to the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP).

According to spokesperson for the WPS Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad, their weekly monitoring of Chinese vessels revealed a mix of boats belonging to the Chinese Coast Guard (CCGV) and People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) across the flashpoint waters.
In Ayungin Shoal, there were five CCG and four PLAN vessels, while in Bajo de Masinloc, there were eight CCG and four PLAN boats roaming around.
Meanwhile, Escoda Shoal had one PLAN boat in its waters, while the Pag-asa Islands had three CCG boats and two PLAN vessels.

The West Philippine Sea refers to the maritime areas on the western side of the Philippine archipelago, including the Luzon Sea and the waters around, within, and adjacent to the Kalayaan Island Group and Bajo de Masinloc.
In 2016, the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague ruled in favor of the Philippines over China's claims in the South China Sea, saying that it had "no legal basis."
China has refused to recognize the decision. —VAL, GMA News

articles.summary: Bookmark this page for Rappler's comprehensive coverage of Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial at the Senate

blocks.text: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.

There are four articles of impeachment against Duterte involving alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery of Department of Education officials, and grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.

Only 21 out of 24 senator-judges are physically present. Senator Bato dela Rosa remains in hiding as he faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, Senator Jinggoy Estrada has been detained and suspended in connection with a plunder case, and Senator Rodante Marcoleta surrendered to authorities as he also faces a plunder case.
On this page, we bring you the latest updates, analyses, videos, and photos as the trial of the Vice President unfolds.

articles.title: What’s an ‘investment ombudsman,’ Boying Remulla’s second-year initiative?
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla says his second year will focus on recovery to help the country’s economy bounce back 'by removing the corruption that holds it back'

blocks.text: OMB. File photo of Ombudsman Jesus Crispin 'Boying' Remulla.
Jire Carreon/Rappler
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla says his second year will focus on recovery to help the country’s economy bounce back 'by removing the corruption that holds it back'

items: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla plans to establish an 'investment ombudsman' to help combat corruption and improve the economy by providing a channel for investors to report bribery and regulatory abuses.
The initiative aims to address issues like regulatory capture, which leads to inflated prices and hinders small businesses, ultimately affecting job creation and economic growth.
Remulla's project aligns with the Ombudsman's constitutional mandate and builds on previous efforts to enhance investment and governance in the Philippines.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Ombudsman Jesus Crispin “Boying” Remulla said he would establish an “investment ombudsman” as he starts his second year as the country’s top anti-graft official.

In his first annual report, Remulla said the Ombudsman’s work would now transition from exacting accountability to recovery to help the country’s economy bounce back “by removing the corruption that holds it back.”
Following his appointment in October 2025, the Office of the Ombudsman filed 39 cases in connection with the flood control corruption controversy.

“Corruption does not only steal from the treasury. It steals from the economy. Ang investor na hiningan ng lagay ay hindi na babalik. At ang trabahong dala sana niya, hindi na rin darating,” Remulla said on Monday, October 12. (Investors who were asked bribes will not return. And the jobs that they could bring will no longer come.)

blocks.caption: What’s an ‘investment ombudsman,’ Boying Remulla’s second-year initiative?

blocks.text: Here are some initial details of Remulla’s project:

What will it do? Remulla said the investment ombudsman will be a channel where local and foreign investors can “report any public official who demands a bribe, sits on a permit, or abuses regulatory power.”

In September, when Remulla first mentioned his plan in a radio show, the Anti-Red Tape Authority said it would be a “timely and strategic reform,” as it would reinforce compliance with the Ease of Doing Business Law and encourage government agencies to prioritize ease of doing business as a cornerstone of governance.
Why the need for it? Remulla said he would stop regulatory capture, which happens when regulatory agencies end up serving the firms they are supposed to police.
According to Remulla, examples of the effects of regulatory capture include bloated power rates, as well as high prices of rice and onions as few players hoard import permits.
He said this could also impact small businesses, which may be unable to open without paying fixers to expedite permits and navigate other unnecessary requirements.
Remulla said addressing bribery could minimize business costs.
“Kapag bumaba ang gastos, bababa ang presyo, dadami ang negosyo, at dadami ang trabaho,” he added. (If costs are down, there will be lower prices, as well as more businesses and jobs.)

In 2027, Remulla said he planned to convene regulators from every industry to hold the Philippine Regulatory Summit to identify regulatory gaps, overlapping functions, procedures vulnerable to corruption, and opportunities for digitization of government transactions.

Is it part of the Ombudsman’s constitutional mandate? Remulla cited Article XI, Section 13(7) of the 1987 Constitution, which provides that the Ombudsman can “determine the cause of inefficiency, red tape, mismanagement, fraud, and corruption in the Government and make recommendations for their elimination and the observance of high standards of ethics and efficiency.”
Have there been previous “investment ombudsman” initiatives? Among those who formed an investment ombudsman team was former ombudsman Conchita Carpio-Morales in 2014.

In a primer available on the Ombudsman website, it was said the team’s purpose was to expedite resolution of investor issues and concerns, encourage local and foreign investments in the country and improve global competitiveness, and assist in attaining the national goal of “inclusive growth and poverty reduction.”

In 1999, then-president Joseph Estrada signed an executive order to create a position for an investment ombudsman, which was under the direct supervision of the chairman of the Board of Investments. Months later, it was transferred to the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) before going to the then Economic Coordinating Council.
Former trade secretaries Peter Favila (Arroyo administration) and Gregory Domingo (Aquino administration) attempted to revive the position. – Rappler.com

articles.title: ‘Universal appeal’: Celebrity Traitors producer reveals secrets to its success
articles.summary:
Over 10m people have tuned in for episodes of new season of BBC hit as mass TV audiences become increasingly rare

For the celebrities chosen as traitors in the BBC’s juggernaut reality show,…

blocks.text: For the celebrities chosen as traitors in the BBC’s juggernaut reality show, the task is simple – kill off fellow contestants without getting caught.

Yet with the new series of Celebrity Traitors once again attracting huge audiences, its UK producers are delighting in one of the show’s more wholesome qualities – its popularity is staving off the death of television’s ability to unite the nation.

“It’s very difficult to get people to watch programmes, and there is a huge joy coming up with something that a very large amount of people watch,” Stephen Lambert, head of the Celebrity Traitors producer Studio Lambert, told the Radio Times.
“The show has universal appeal … It has established itself as ‘appointment-to-view TV’,” he added.
Despite its appeal, however, Lambert may still struggle to attract the man he revealed to be his dream contestant: Tom Cruise.

More than 10 million people have tuned in to watch some episodes, well in excess of half the viewers watching TV during the show’s time slot. It is also pulling younger viewers away from other devices and on to the sofa, with 1.6 million people aged between 16 and 34 tuning in for this series’ premiere.

blocks.caption: ‘We get that wonderful extra sneaky peak behind the facade of celebrity’. Photograph: Euan Cherry/BBC/Studio Lambert

blocks.text: In doing so, it has bucked a long-running trend that has seen mass TV audiences become increasingly rare. The arrival of streamers, digital platforms and smartphones have ensured such viewing figures have become the preserve of the Olympics, England World Cup matches and the odd breakthrough hit.

The success of The Traitors has inevitably spawned similar formats based on deceit and questionable detective skills, as producers attempt to replicate its allure. Lambert said that whether it was the celebrity edition or the regular series of The Traitors, the secret to its success came down to two words: “Dramatic irony.”
“It’s the engine of The Traitors,” he said. “It’s about the pleasure that we know more than the protagonists – we know who is lying. And it’s fun to try and watch people work out who the liars are.”

When it comes to the celebrity edition, he said viewers delighted in seeing famous faces uncomfortable as they “have so little control” over events. “It’s such an immersive game that people get caught up in it, and show how they really are,” he said.

Lambert confirmed that casting for Celebrity Traitors was not difficult because its popularity meant that the names who agreed to go into the traitors’ castle were also fans. Producers have previously noted the show does not face the usual challenges of attracting names to formats that ask them to eat bugs or train for weeks on end.

Not only would Cruise be a tough man to pin down, Lambert also said securing sports stars continues to be a perennial problem for casting directors. Sports men and women not only have gruelling schedules, but their media activities are guarded closely by personal agents and their clubs.
When asked about dream contestants, Lambert said: “Tom Cruise, maybe? And we would like to have a big sports star. But if they are an active one, they have commitments.”

Shows similar in style to The Traitors have been attempted, such as Channel 4’s The Inheritance or ITV’s The Neighbourhood, though both networks and production companies usually bridle at any suggestion that their latest reality format amounts to their new spin on The Traitors.
Even the most experienced TV insiders freely admit that productions that were fun to make and have found audiences overseas come with no guarantee of success.

“If anyone tells you what the secret is, they are not in full command of reality,” said Jonathan Glazier, a former head of BBC light entertainment. “Don’t you think if we knew, every show would be a Traitors?

“It’s just a joy to sit back and marvel at the duplicity and wonder why the faithful can’t see the traitors for who they are! That said, the cliffhangers are so brilliantly executed … and with the celeb version we get that wonderful extra sneaky peak behind the facade of celebrity.
“It’s a joy to watch and any team that tries to imitate that kind of simplistic perfection is going to come a cropper.”

articles.title: Women ‘more likely to be told autoimmune conditions are psychological’
articles.summary:
Cambridge University study suggests stark gender divide in misdiagnosis, with women also waiting longer for treatment

Women with autoimmune conditions are up to 74% more likely than men to…

blocks.text: Women with autoimmune conditions are up to 74% more likely than men to be told their symptoms are psychological or psychosomatic, and face much longer waits for a diagnosis and treatment, a study suggests.
Hundreds of millions of people – about one in 10 globally – are affected by autoimmune conditions, which can cause a range of health issues including fatigue, muscle pain and rashes.
But research by the University of Cambridge and University of East Anglia suggests a stark gender divide when it comes to how signs of the conditions are handled by doctors.

Women are more likely to have their conditions wrongly attributed to psychiatric causes, more likely to have symptoms misdiagnosed as psychosomatic, and more likely to experience delays in getting a diagnosis, according to the study.
The lead author, Melanie Sloan, said: “The damage caused to women by these types of misdiagnosis can be very long lasting in terms of trusting doctors and their own self-esteem.”

Sloan, a researcher in the department of public health and primary care at Cambridge and UEA, said some women were forced to wait years before finally getting a diagnosis, causing long delays to treatment for their condition.
The study, published in the Lancet eClinicalMedicine journal, included more than 6,600 people with autoimmune conditions. Most were female and from the UK.

Patients listed their main condition, with almost a quarter of the women having autoimmune thyroid disease, which can cause the gland to become underactive – known as Hashimoto’s disease – or overactive, known as Graves’ disease. Hashimoto’s disease can cause weight gain, hair loss, fatigue and joint pain, while the symptoms of Graves’ disease include bulging eyes, palpitations and weight loss.
One in seven women in the study had systemic lupus, which can cause tiredness, rashes and muscle pain.
Among male patients, rheumatoid arthritis, vasculitis and antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), also known as “sticky blood” syndrome, were the most common conditions.

blocks.caption: Women were almost 46% more likely to report having received a psychiatric misdiagnosis, and nearly 74% more likely to have a psychosomatic misdiagnosis.  Photograph: MBI/Alamy

blocks.text: Researchers found 43% of women reported being told their condition was down to a psychiatric cause compared with a third of men (33%).
A third (34%) of women also reported having symptoms misdiagnosed as psychosomatic – meaning they were triggered or worsened by stress or anxiety – compared with 22% of men.

Overall, after accounting for factors including age, disease group, continent and household finances, researchers said women were 46% more likely to report having received a psychiatric misdiagnosis, and 74% more likely to report a psychosomatic misdiagnosis than men.

Researchers also found women reported much longer periods between the onset of symptoms and receiving a diagnosis, as well as more healthcare consultations. Among men, the most frequently reported time to diagnosis was less than three months. Among women, it was one to two years.
Autoimmune conditions, which happen when the immune system attacks the body by mistake, can be complex to diagnose as they often present with symptoms common in the wider population.
after newsletter promotion
The study team said “broader diagnostic challenges affect both sexes” but “females may face additional disadvantages”.
They added: “Historical biases in medicine may persist, including positioning females as less credible and emotional reporters of symptoms than males.”
Sloan said the findings “highlight that psychological or mental health explanations can be given too soon”.
She added: “This is true for both sexes, but our study suggests that females may be particularly vulnerable to these types of misdiagnoses.
“It is really important that symptoms are not automatically assumed to be psychological and for doctors to just say, ‘I believe you,’ to patients with symptoms that the doctors cannot see.”

Shaista Tayabali, a patient affected by an autoimmune condition who was part of the research team and a co-author of the study, said: “The differences between the sexes in misdiagnoses for people with autoimmune diseases is stark.
“The fact that females reported higher rates of psychiatric and psychosomatic misdiagnoses than males … suggests that historical gender biases remain a challenging aspect of the diagnostic journey.
“Although labels such as hysteria are outdated, and fortunately rarely used nowadays, as women we still often have a harder time having our symptoms believed and therefore addressed accurately.”

articles.title: ‘Super app’ aimed at UK students uses servers owned by Chinese firm on US blacklist
articles.summary:
ZyMix platform has contract with Tencent, which US alleges has links to People’s Liberation Army

A new messaging and payment “super app” marketed at British students uses servers owned by a…

blocks.text: A new messaging and payment “super app” marketed at British students uses servers owned by a Chinese company that has been put on a US military blacklist for its alleged affiliation to the People’s Liberation Army.

ZyMix, which is being pushed on university campuses as the UK’s first super app designed “for gen Z”, combining chat, payments and community features, has a contract with a German-based subsidiary of Tencent Holdings, a Chinese conglomerate in Shenzhen.
Tencent Holdings was added in January 2026 to the US Department of Defense’s (DoD) list of Chinese military companies, which is formally known as the section 1260H list.
The citation on the DoD list says that the company, which is a gaming and social media conglomerate, is indirectly affiliated to the Chinese People’s Liberation Army.
The blacklist is part of a US attempt to counteract what it regards as Beijing’s efforts to increase its military power by using technology from Chinese firms, universities and research programmes.
The DoD is prohibited from entering into, renewing or extending contracts for goods, services or technology with any entity on the list although wider sanctions are not automatic.

A Tencent spokesperson said: “Tencent’s inclusion on this list is clearly a mistake. We are not a military company or supplier. Unlike sanctions or export controls, this listing has no impact on our business. We will nonetheless work with the Department of Defense to address any misunderstanding.”
China’s footprint in higher education in the UK has become a controversial issue. MI5 recently warned British universities to cut ties with the China General Technology Research Institute.

The domestic intelligence service claimed it was secretly channelling funding from Beijing’s intelligence apparatus to UK-linked academics to improve the technical espionage capabilities of China’s ministry of state security.
The link between the Chinese-owned infrastructure and ZyMix was initially disclosed in the company’s privacy policy at the time of its launch last week.

The document, which is legally required, said that Tencent (Frankfurt) stored user-generated content and messages. After the Guardian approached the company, the privacy policy was rewritten and mention of Tencent was removed.

The policy now states that users’ personal data is stored and processed primarily in the United Kingdom and the EU, adding that “some of our service providers are located in other countries, including the United States”.

It goes on to say that “auxiliary infrastructure providers, hosted in the EU, receive only encrypted user messages and limited technical data, such as technical statistics, licence validation when the app starts”.

A spokesperson said: “As a newly launched startup, we are updating our privacy notice as we develop our services, including clarifying that Tencent, Twilio and the other providers concerned are used solely for performance testing.”

The spokesperson added: “Our agreement is with Tencent Cloud Europe BV, which we use for auxiliary services, rather than as the provider that stores ZyMix user data. We take our obligations under UK data protection law seriously.”
The new privacy policy invites those who wish to know the identity of their suppliers to request the information from the company.
In response to a request from the Guardian, Tarique Ghaffur, a former assistant commissioner at the Metropolitan police, who described himself as a security consultant for ZyMix, responded.

He said: “We have reviewed your request as against our private privacy [sic] you mentioned. Unfortunately, at the present time for reasons of commercial confidentiality, contractual obligations and legal privileges, we are not able to provide you with the requested information.”

Fraser Sampson, a professor of security and national governance and formerly the UK’s biometrics and surveillance camera commissioner, said he was “sceptical when ‘commercial confidentiality’ arguments are used to duck basic policy questions and amending policy on the fly is never reassuring”.

He added: “When companies ask us for our personal data, they should expect us to ask them where it’s being kept, for what purpose(s) and who they’re going to share it with – and be prepared to answer fully.”
Sam Dunning, the director of the UK-China Transparency NGO, said: “There are serious questions about whether ZyMix have taken due care before launching this product.”
A spokesperson for ZyMix said: “Whilst still in its beta stage, the ZyMix app has been developed to fully comply with all UK data, privacy and financial regulations.”

ZyMix is heavily targeting the university market and is offering £200 to £400 a month to people who agree to be brand ambassadors on campuses. Staff roles have also been advertised in the UK by ZyMix for Mandarin-speaking applicants.

One advert on LinkedIn for the job of operations manager (Mandarin speaking) required “excellent written and verbal communication skills in both English and Mandarin (required for daily communication with the China team)”.

Separately, a distinct company appeared to be recruiting on behalf of ZyMix on WeChat, the Chinese instant messaging service, saying: “The product, R&D, design and testing team is in Greater China, with branch-company bases covering: Taipei / Shenzhen / Guangzhou / Hangzhou / Chengdu / Zhengzhou.”

Ghaffur said that Flicknmix, the UK company that publishes the ZyMix app, “does not have any subsidiaries or branch offices in China. Our aim is to create opportunities within the UK”. A spokesperson for ZyMix described it as “British born”.

articles.title: [Vantage Point] Holiday dividend or market coal? What GCash could deliver by Christmas
articles.summary: Holiday dividend or market coal? What GCash could deliver by Christmas.

blocks.text: Will retail investors unwrap a plump holiday dividend this Yuletide season, or find a lump of market coal tucked inside their stockings?
With Christmas lanterns already lighting up storefronts and GCash set to make its market debut at P6.60 a share, that very question has filled our inbox.

Many readers are tempted by the prospect of owning a slice of an app they use daily to send aguinaldo (Christmas money) and settle holiday bills — and by the tantalizing wish that a quick IPO pop might bankroll their Christmas spending.
In response, Vantage Point ran a forensic valuation exercise to separate holiday cheer from cold, hard arithmetic.

Before anyone adds GCash shares to their holiday wish list, one essential qualification is in order. What follows is strictly an analytical exercise prompted by reader inquiries. It is neither a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold GCASH (the company’s ticker name), nor is it intended to sway trading behavior.

Share prices are inherently volatile beasts, particularly amid the turbulent opening weeks of a high-profile listing. Everyday investors must always make decisions tailored to their individual financial circumstances, risk tolerance, and independent research.
With that caveat firmly established, our numbers suggest an upward bias during GCash’s opening week of trading.

GCASH makes its formal debut on the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on October 20 at P6.60. Our baseline scenario places the stock between P7.00 and P7.70 after its first full week on the boards, with roughly P7.40 serving as a sensible midpoint. That would represent a neat 12% gain from the offer price.

Under a bearish scenario, the shares could stumble toward P5.90 to P6.50. Conversely, an avalanche of pent-up demand from institutions and retail accounts could lift them toward the P7.80 to P8.80 corridor.

Why lean optimistic at the opening bell? Institutional bookbuilding was heavily oversubscribed, and more than 20 cornerstone investors locked in P36.5 billion in commitments. Big accounts that were scaled back or shut out during allocation often return as eager secondary-market buyers.

Moreover, GCash commands an advantage almost unprecedented for a domestic listing: an immense, captive audience. With 41.5 million monthly active users, it can present this equity offer straight to a population that already trusts its digital wallet.

Through GStocks PH, everyday retail investors can enter the fray with a board lot of just 100 shares, requiring an accessible P660 outlay at the IPO price. (READ: Want to buy GCash shares? How retail investors can join the IPO)
Yet early excitement should never be mistaken for durable value. A good portion of retail buyers will have subscribed solely to capture a quick first-day pop.

If GCASH swiftly marches toward P7.50 or P8.00, early participants sitting on double-digit paper gains may choose to cash out immediately. The opening week will inevitably become a tug-of-war between under allocated funds looking to accumulate shares and profit-takers eager to ring the register.
That makes October 27 (a full week after initial listing) a far more telling milestone than October 20.

If GCASH stays comfortably above P7.00 after several sessions of heavy churn, our base-to-bull thesis will gain genuine credibility. If it tests P8.00 and holds that ground despite waves of profit-taking, underlying institutional support is likely much stronger than conservative models assume.

On the flip side, if the stock slumps and lingers below its P6.60 offer price once official price-stabilization support winds down, it will serve as a stark warning that blowout bookbuilding numbers failed to translate into lasting market demand.
Then comes the bigger question dominating our inbox: Where might GCash settle once the Christmas holiday arrives?
Our valuation modeling outlines three distinct paths by year-end:

items: The Bearish Case (P5.50 – P6.30): Cooling market momentum and slowing core operations compress multiples.
The Base Case (P7.30 – P8.20): A balanced performance centered at P7.70, delivering a steady post-listing appreciation of roughly 17%.
The Bullish Case (P8.80 – P10.00): Sustained retail appetite and fresh foreign inflows push valuations back toward the original ceiling.

blocks.text: These boundaries are anchored strictly in valuation arithmetic. At P6.60, Mynt carries an equity value of roughly P442 billion, or approximately 25.6 times its 2025 net profit of P17.25 billion. If full-year 2026 earnings reach around P21 billion — in line with its first-half performance — earnings per share across roughly 66.9 billion post-offer shares would sit near P0.31 to P0.32. At a P7.70 midpoint, GCASH would trade at roughly 24 times prospective earnings.

While that multiple commands a premium over traditional Philippine conglomerates, it remains defensible for a dominant, profitable fintech expanding into micro-lending, savings, insurance, and investments.
Yet the bears have compelling arguments. In the first half of 2026, Mynt’s net profit grew by just 7%, while core EBITDA dipped 4% and margins narrowed to 27.3%.

Furthermore, passive interest earned on its P68.6-billion cash balance jumped 45% to P2.56 billion, masking softening operating earnings. Serious investors must watch whether core platform revenue regains momentum rather than relying on bank deposit interest to carry the bottom line.

External variables could easily scramble these projections. A sudden downturn across the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE), shifts in foreign capital flows, currency headwinds, or geopolitical shocks could overpower company-level fundamentals.
Even so, setting these benchmarks gives investors concrete markers to track. Our primary checkpoint is P7.00 to P7.70 one week in, followed by our year-end base band of P7.30 to P8.20.
Will GCash provide extra cash for Noche Buena (Christmas Eve feast)? Perhaps. But treating an initial public offering like a guaranteed holiday bonus is a dangerous mistake.
The true test begins on October 20, when millions of Filipinos who trust GCash with their daily funds discover whether trusting it with their investment capital yields the very same satisfaction.
I welcome your views on these and other issues where decisions made in power shape the country’s economic future.

articles.title: Business leaders, consumers demand solutions to Visayas power crisis at Cebu summit
articles.summary: Repeated power interruptions have drawn concern from domestic and international clients about Cebu's capability to support business needs, possibly affecting future transactions and partnerships,…

blocks.text: POWER. Government officials and industry experts gathered for the Cebu Energy Summit on October 12, 2026, to discuss solutions and initiatives that will address the province's rising power demands and struggle for reliable energy.
Cebu Provincial Government

Repeated power interruptions have drawn concern from domestic and international clients about Cebu's capability to support business needs, possibly affecting future transactions and partnerships, says a business leader

items: Business leaders and civic groups in Cebu are urging government officials for improved transparency and long-term solutions to the ongoing power crisis, which has led to significant outages and interruptions affecting local industries.
The Cebu Chamber of Commerce and Industry reported that repeated power interruptions are causing productivity losses and raising concerns among clients about Cebu's business capabilities.

Consumer welfare advocates are calling for affordable and reliable electricity, emphasizing the need for diversified energy projects and improvements to the grid to address supply issues, while cautioning against reliance on coal as a solution.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

CEBU, Philippines – Business leaders, civic society groups, and concerned citizens on Monday, October 12, called on government officials for better transparency and reliable long-term solutions amid the Visayas power crisis.

They made the call at the Cebu Energy Summit held after months of power interruptions and outages due to an unavailability of supply from the region’s power plants. The National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) disclosed in a September situation report that more than 1,500 megawatts were unavailable due to forced plant outages and reduced operating capacities even with imports from Luzon.

Bernard Sia, Cebu Chamber of Commerce and Industry (CCCI) vice president for Cebu Business Mobilization, shared during the summit that many industries in the province are unable to shift to backup power when a power interruption occurs.

“For construction, [CCCI] members told us that interruptions affect electrically powered equipment, pumps, lighting, site offices and other activities, which can mean work stoppages, lower productivity, and delays,” Sia said.

Sia added that the repeated interruptions have drawn concern from domestic and international clients about Cebu’s capability to support business needs, possibly affecting future transactions and partnerships.

On top of affected trade, the CCCI reported that businesses, especially small and medium enterprises, have been forced to absorb additional costs, ranging from generator and fuel procurements to repairs and equipment protection.
Asked about the business outlook for Cebu amid the power crisis, Sia told Rappler on the sidelines of the summit that some businesses may face closures next year.
“It’s not going to be a good picture, but, you know, as always, we just want to be able to make sure that all businesses survive,” he said.

The CCCI called on officials to provide better information on the schedule of the outages and stronger reliability from the grid through adequate power generation, sufficient energy reserves, and better distribution.
Cebu Governor Pamela Baricuatro highlighted these concerns in her speech during the summit.

“Every day, brownout means lost income for small businesses, disrupted work, or another difficult night for a family. For our hospitals and essential services, dependable electricity is critical to keeping people safe,” the governor said.
Department of Energy (DOE) and NGCP data showed that Cebu carries the largest share of the Visayas grid’s manual load dropping allocation — at 42%, based on the province’s demand share.

Manual load dropping or rotational power interruption happens when there is limited electricity supply or high demand from consumers. NGCP coordinates with electric cooperatives and distribution utilities to temporarily cut off electricity in non-critical sectors like households to maintain the grid’s reliability and prevent a system collapse.
Cebu Electricity Rights Advocates (CERA) lead convenor Nathaniel Chua said that consumer welfare should to be at the center of all future energy policy decisions.

“Cebuanos deserve electricity that is fair, affordable, reliable and dependable — not power that comes with unpredictable costs and recurring threats of supply shortages,” Chua said in a statement sent to Rappler.

In September, electricity rates through major distributors like Visayan Electric, which serves the major Cebu cities, were at P14.89 per kilowatt-hour for residential areas, a sharp increase from P12.79 per kilowatt-hour in January.

CERA urged government officials to ensure that electricity bills are affordable and reflect transparent, long-term power contracts and reasonable costs, rather than Wholesale Electricity Spot Market (WESM) price spikes or unexplained and unannounced pass-through charges.
Chua said that Cebu’s energy problem can be addressed with more supply as a long-term solution through more diversified energy projects and sufficient ancillary services and reserve power.
“For the short term, we need to improve our NGCP lines so that we can immediately import power from Luzon,” Chua added.
Teody Navea, secretary of Sanlakas Cebu, echoed CERA’s demands, urging the Cebu provincial government to take a people-centered approach amid the Super El Niño phenomenon.

Navea warned that the vulnerability of the Visayas grid would invite proposals for coal plants, despite the moratorium on new coal-fired power plants since 2020. The moratorium, however, does not prevent coal power proponents from applying for non-coverage.

“To look at coal as a viable baseload solution during extreme weather events is not just short-sighted but a dangerous step backward. Coal is not the remedy for our grid instability — coal is precisely the problem,” Navea said.
Sanlakas Cebu called on officials to seek greener power generation and affordable renewable energy sources. – Rappler.com

articles.title: ASEAN to discuss tackling transboundary haze ahead of November summit
articles.summary: Southeast Asian foreign ministers will during a meeting next month seek to tackle the transboundary haze blanketing parts of the region, ASEAN chair the Philippines said on Tuesday.

blocks.text: Published October 13, 2026 11:45am
A drone view shows St. Joseph's Cathedral shrouded in haze from wildfires, in Pontianak, West Kalimantan province, Indonesia, September 15, 2026. REUTERS/Ajeng Dinar Ulfiana/File

MANILA/KUALA LUMPUR - Southeast Asian foreign ministers will during a meeting next month seek to tackle the transboundary haze blanketing parts of the region, ASEAN chair the Philippines said on Tuesday.

Forest and land fires that have raged for months in Indonesia have in recent weeks caused thick haze in Singapore and in Malaysia, which closed schools in several states last week after air pollution hit unhealthy levels.
The wildfires, mainly on the islands of Sumatra and Borneo, are Indonesia's most intense in 11 years.

"It's in the agenda," Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs spokesperson on ASEAN Dominic Xavier Imperial said on Tuesday, referring to the preparatory foreign ministers' meetings in November ahead of the summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations
Malaysian Foreign Minister Mohamad Hasan on Monday said he would raise the haze issue with ASEAN, noting that the bloc's existing mechanisms to deal with natural disasters did not include haze.
Malaysia has previously offered assistance to Indonesia to combat fires.

Firefighting attempts in many areas were complicated by poor visibility, accessibility issues and a lack of suitable conditions for cloud seeding, Mohamad said, citing discussions with his Indonesian counterpart. —Reuters

articles.title: Sara Duterte denies owning lot NBI tied to her asset declarations
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte has denied owning a lot that the National Bureau of Investigation claims to be one of the properties in her statement of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN), and…

blocks.text: October 13, 2026 | 11:45am
Images show footage of properties linked to the Vice President and Davao City Rep. Paolo Duterte during a presentation by the National Bureau of Investigation.
NBI images

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte has denied owning a lot that the National Bureau of Investigation claims to be one of the properties in her statement of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN), and accused the bureau of misleading the public.

The denial came a day after NBI Director Melvin Matibag presented the agency’s initial findings on alleged discrepancies in the declared property values of Duterte and her brother Rep. Paolo Duterte (Davao City, 1st District), based on on-the-ground inspections by NBI agents in Davao City.

Duterte’s SALN declarations are also currently at issue in the Senate impeachment trial, where the court has been shown stacks of financial and corporate records that prosecutors claim is proof of her unexplained, undeclared and disproportionate wealth.

“The lot in the photo that he said is in my Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth is not mine,” Duterte said in a statement in Filipino. She did not identify the specific property she was alluding to.
Duterte said it was alarming that the NBI was using its operations “for activities with no clear benefit to the public.”

She said such “deception of the public” was the reason the NBI was removed from the list of witnesses the prosecution would present in the impeachment proceedings. She cited what she described as allegations that the bureau had again put forward questionable evidence, as with the affidavit of dismissed police officer Rodulfo Gracioso Jr.
The prosecution has confirmed that it would be presenting no more witnesses after forensic financial analyst Alexander Cabrera, who is the prosecution's last witness for its case-in-chief.

Citing a need to speed up proceedings, prosecutors have trimmed their witness list several times, including forgoing 15 of 27 witnesses originally planned for the confidential funds charge, and last week dropped the Article III or bribery charge.
NBI claims Duterte property worth up to P60 million

At a briefing on Monday, October 12, Matibag claimed a property in Catigan, Davao City, declared as agricultural land worth P890,000, was estimated at P50 million to P60 million after it was inspected.
Matibag said the Duterte family has 121 properties in Davao City and Davao del Norte, 24 of which belong to the vice president and are under investigation.
About 14 properties had been identified from the vice president's SALNs for field inspection, according to the NBI.

The probe, Matibag said, follows a pattern the bureau established from Gracioso’s affidavit, in which money was allegedly put into land banking, as he said was the practice with former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
Matibag said the NBI would submit initial findings to the Ombudsman and the Department of Justice, possibly within the week, and denied the investigation was politically motivated.

Gracioso, whom the national police confirmed served on Velasco’s security detail, has alleged that he delivered more than P2 billion in cash to Duterte in more than 20 transactions, ranging from P20 million to P50 million each. He also claimed deliveries to Paolo Duterte and former President Rodrigo Duterte between 2018 and 2020.
Duterte has denied knowing Gracioso or receiving money from him.

articles.title: Chel Diokno: Evidence vs. Sara Duterte based on independent, verifiable facts
articles.summary: House prosecutor and Akbayan party-list Rep. Chel Diokno on Monday said the prosecution's evidence against Vice President Sara Duterte was based on independent and verifiable facts, rejecting claims…

blocks.text: Published October 13, 2026 11:37am

House prosecutor and Akbayan party-list Rep. Chel Diokno on Monday said the prosecution's evidence against Vice President Sara Duterte was based on independent and verifiable facts, rejecting claims that the allegations against her were fabricated.

Diokno made the statement when Senator Lito Lapid asked what the public should make of the extensive evidence presented by the prosecution, including Duterte's Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs), bank transactions and deposits, insurance policies, business interests and income records involving her and her husband.

“Madali po kasi ang magpanggap ang isang official na simpleng tao lang siya, kumakain lang sa carinderia, malinis, wala naman na tinatago sa SALN. Pero pag titignan po sa isyu ng Article 2 on unexplained wealth, doon po tayo magkakaalaman,” Diokno said.

(It is easy for a public official to pretend to be an ordinary person who eats at carinderias, has nothing to hide and has a clean SALN. But when we examine Article II on unexplained wealth, that is when the truth will come out.)
Diokno stressed that the prosecution's case did not rely solely on witness testimonies but was also supported by financial documents obtained from independent sources.

“Because we are not just looking at the witnesses here. We are looking at the documents and numbers. Attorney Cabrera looked at bank records from the Anti-Money Laundering Council, Bureau of Internal Revenue, Securities and Exchange Commission," Diokno said.
"And the bank documents were submitted by the banks to the Senate court, not the prosecution. That is why we can say that these are independent facts verifiable by everybody,” he added.
He was referring to the testimony of lawyer and accountant Alex Cabrera, who conducted a forensic examination of the financial records of Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio.

Cabrera concluded that based on a "conservative" assessment, the couple had at least P817 million in alleged unexplained wealth, with the amount potentially reaching P1.5 billion due to assets purportedly left undeclared in their joint SALNs.

Earlier on Monday, October 12, the 38th day of her impeachment trial, Duterte claimed during a press conference that the evidence against her had been fabricated and that the impeachment case was falling apart.

Meanwhile, House prosecutor and Manila Rep. Joel Chua challenged Duterte's defense team to seek the dismissal of the impeachment charges through a demurrer to evidence if it believed the prosecution had failed to establish its case.

“If they believe that our evidence is weak and we haven’t proven anything, then I challenge them to file demurrer to evidence. That is being done in a regular court. They can file that so this will be resolved earlier,” Chua said in an interview on Super Radyo dzBB.

A demurrer to evidence is a legal remedy through which an accused may seek the dismissal of a case after the prosecution rests, arguing that the evidence presented is insufficient to sustain a conviction.
Chua maintained that the prosecution's allegations were supported by Duterte's own declarations, including information she disclosed or allegedly failed to disclose in her SALNs.

“Our Constitution clearly states that the Vice President, President and Cabinet Secretaries are not allowed to have business interest, either directly or indirectly. But she declared business interests in her SALN [while she was] already the Vice President,” Chua said.
He was referring to GenCorp Foods Corporation, which Duterte listed among her business interests.
“Maliwanag na po yun na paglabag, not just an ordinary law, but the Constitution at that,” Chua added.
(That is clearly a violation, not just of an ordinary law but of the Constitution itself.)— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: FAST FACTS: The military’s modernization push
articles.summary: Delays in the first two phases of the Revised AFP Modernization Program have prompted the Marcos administration to extend funding until 2034, even as the law is set to expire in 2027

blocks.text: Delays in the first two phases of the Revised AFP Modernization Program have prompted the Marcos administration to extend funding until 2034, even as the law is set to expire in 2027

items: The Armed Forces of the Philippines increased its spending for external defense through the Revised AFP Modernization Program.
The program has faced delays and funding constraints, prompting calls for a more flexible modernization approach to better address evolving defense needs.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) has amped up its spending to fulfill its external defense mandate.

In December 2012, the late former president Benigno Aquino III signed the law on the Revised AFP Modernization Program (RAFPMP) to provide the military with new platforms and assets and phase out obsolete ones in its inventory.
Thirteen years into the program and a year before its legislated end, what upgrades has the AFP seen?

The RAFPMP was originally divided into three five-year phases called Horizons, according to the Congressional Policy and Budget Research Department of the House of Representatives. Each horizon focused on:

items: Horizon 1 (2013-2017) – internal security operations and establishing capability in internal security, humanitarian assistance, and disaster response while building up defense in the West Philippine Sea
Horizon 2 (2018-2022) – improved territorial defense to address security concerns in the West Philippine Sea
Horizon 3 (2023-2028) – strengthening archipelagic defense, including awareness and control of air and sea domains and intelligence

blocks.text: In 2024, the Marcos administration reimagined Horizon 3 into Re-Horizon 3 and lengthened its period to 10 years instead of the original five years. This came after it reviewed the overdue contracts from previous phases.
This caused an adjustment in the acquisition list because of prior implementation delays and funding constraints.

Under Republic Act No. 10349, the program is given a separate budget from the Department of National Defense (DND) and the AFP in the General Appropriations Act. In 2026, it received a P40-billion allocation. The program may also receive additional funding from unprogrammed appropriations. In 2026, military modernization was allocated P50 billion in unprogrammed funds.

The DND may also undergo multi-year contracts through the Multi-Year Contractual Authority, making it possible for payments to be made through installments over several years. The DND can also enter into government-to-government agreements to secure development assistance loans to finance major acquisitions.

In the first two phases, the program spending was slightly higher than its allocation. In Horizon 1, P9.6 billion was spent, more than its allotted budget of P7.5 billion. Meanwhile, in Horizon 2, the program spent P45.1 billion.
In 2022, the program received a bump in budget to support defense efforts amid the growing presence of Chinese vessels in the West Philippine Sea.
The program’s final phase is expected to have a budget of P189 billion.
In the program’s first two horizons, 151 projects were approved.
Of the 53 approved projects in Horizon 1, a total of 36 were completed, according to a DND report in 2025.

In Horizon 2, only 22 out of 98 were completed. During the 2022 Senate budget deliberations, former AFP deputy chief of staff Vice Admiral Rommel Anthony Reyes attributed the delays to the agency’s funding constraints.
Among the major acquisitions during Horizon 1 were the following:

items: FA-50 light-lift fighter jets
Multi-purpose assault craft
Jose Rizal-class frigates
BRP Tarlac
BRP Davao del Sur

blocks.text: Under Horizon 2, the AFP’s major purchases included:

items: Miguel Malvar-class frigates (BRP Miguel Malvar and BRP Diego Silang)
Offshore patrol vessels (Rajah Sulayman class)
Black Hawk utility helicopters
Anti-ship Missile System from BrahMos Aerospace
Sabrah Light Tanks
ATMOS 2000
Unmanned aerial systems (Hermes 900, Hermes 450, and ScanEagle UAS)

blocks.text: In the updated wishlist, some items from the first two horizons were removed because they no longer fit the country’s defense needs, according to then-military chief Andres Centino. He added that some projects were removed due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The items the AFP planned to acquire then under the last phase were multirole fighters, radars, frigates, missile systems, and rescue helicopters, amounting to over P500 billion.

Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. has said the modernization program based on the current law was too rigid and that its horizons were too long. Teodoro suggested referring to Ukraine’s model, which had a faster planning phase.
He said this would help the country adapt and acquire new assets on par with evolving threats, rather than wait for fixed phases. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Of drones, dreams, and endless possibilities for the Philippine Navy
articles.summary: The Philippines’ security sector looks to a future of indigenous drone technology

image.caption: Watch on Facebook

blocks.text: The Philippines’ security sector looks to a future of indigenous drone technology
WESTERN OUTPOST. Philippine soldiers stationed on Likas Island stand guard in June 2025. File photo by Bea Cupin/Rappler
MANILA, Philippines – It was a hot weekend morning at a remote military camp in the Philippine mainland and a few officers and soldiers gathered there were both nervous and excited.

Philippine security and defense personnel were set to test homegrown drone technology. An unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) whizzed across the horizon. A few seconds later, the test mission was done and dusted — and passed with flying colors.
Cheers erupted, congratulations were exchanged. Several observers stood, beaming — this journalist among them.
Rappler was among a handful of people who witnessed the test run. For security reasons, we have withheld other details related to the UAV test and its outcomes.

For soldiers behind the test run, it meant finally being able to breathe easy. For the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), it was a few steps forward into the future of warfare: unmanned systems produced at scale domestically.

To understand why Philippine-made UAVs are important for the AFP, it’s important to acknowledge the gaps that the Army, Air Force, and Navy must bridge to protect the Philippines’ vast spaces from land to air to sea. Maritime coverage is especially critical, given the military’s shift in focus to external defense.

For the Navy, the challenge is clear: there’s a gap between the information that outposts and stations collate through radars and other systems and what needs to be checked with their own eyes, several officers told Rappler.

In some cases, foreign vessels in the Philippines’ maritime spaces would routinely go dark from the Automatic Identification System or AIS. That’s when visual confirmation — through manned or unmanned vessels or aircraft — is needed.

Sending a Navy ship is ideal but not always possible, and there’s the problem of availability and potential travel time. At sea and on land, timeliness is critical to intelligence and domain awareness.

So imagine this future for a military that once lagged way behind its regional neighbors: homegrown UAVs and tech that’s produced locally and for much cheaper than the drones the AFP already procures from foreign partners and allies.
From where we stood in that test run, it’s a future that’s closer to reality than mere imagination.
In October 2025, the Philippine Navy hosted a Drone Warfare Summit for the first time.
The push to pursue an indigenous UAV program and to innovate is spurred by the lessons from a war halfway across the world.

Ukraine has mastered, within just a few years, the technology needed to develop and scale drone warfare in the middle of Russia’s war against it. The Russia-Ukraine war offers another real-world lesson to countries around the globe, according to a study by the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS).

“Equipment attrition rates experienced in the war in Ukraine and the high volume of munitions expended there and in other theaters have spotlighted the challenges that industry faces in generating the manufacturing capacity to meet armed forces’ demands. These and other issues have prompted governments to dedicate attention and resources to develop defense industry strategies and policies,” read a report under its Military Balance+ project.
By the Philippines, for the Philippines
On the ground, the challenges for the Philippines are quite different.

Inside Camp Cape Bojeador in Burgos, Ilocos Norte, for instance, are snapshots of the AFP’s past — armored vehicles, an old Blue Diamond fighter plane, and platforms that were once produced in the country for its own military’s use.

Vicente Blanco III, the now-retired Marine Corps commander who moved the 4th Marine Brigade from southern Mindanao to a province way up north, took pride in touring guests around the military park. It was Blanco who near-singlehandedly curated and sourced the different platforms, saving a handful from the doom of being turned into scrap metal.
We visited the camp in 2024, when he talked aloud about his hopes that one day, the military’s toys will be Philippine-made again.

blocks.caption: VINTAGE AFP. A fighter jet once used by the Blue Diamonds is displayed at Camp Cape Bojeador in this file photo from June 2024. Photo by Bea Cupin/Rappler

blocks.text: Months later, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed into law the Self-Reliant Defense Posture (SRDP) Revitalization Act, which seeks to take off from what his namesake and father, the late dictator, pulled off before he was deposed: tapping local industry to supply the military its ammunition, vehicles, communication platforms, and clothes.

“We lay today the foundation of resilience shaped by our own ingenuity, our own talent, and our unwavering resolve…. Through this act, we can build on its legacy and expand upon that same vision — a defense posture that is independent, dynamic, and geared to the future,” said Marcos in October 2024, as he signed the bill into law.
The Philippines isn’t alone in crafting a dedicated national defense-industrial strategy, according to the IISS study.

A handful of nations that have published their first national defense-industrial strategy are either allies or military partners of the Philippines — the United States, Canada, and New Zealand. Manila is among several countries around the world that updated defense self-reliance plans after a decade-long gap.

Lucie Béraud-Sudreau, in the IISS review, said the push for defense self-reliance as policy “reflects a shock realization of the demands of sustaining modern high-intensity warfare, and the fragility of supply chains that support weapons production.”

The SRDP Revitalization Act is meant to incentivize investments in defense tech and production through tax breaks and government-backed financing while also barring the sale of these weapons, tech, and equipment to private entities.

It also created a new office under the Department of National Defense — the Office of the Undersecretary for Defense Technology Research and Industry Development — which is meant to further the policy, collate data, spur research and development, bridge public and private, and even set up ties with foreign partners.
“To the private sector, it is an invitation to build an enduring defense industry,” said Marcos of the law.

Yet there have been few updates on how the law, which was meant to make it easier for local manufacturers to supply the military its needs, as well as to revive and spur that industry, has boosted local production.

READ FAST FACTS: The military’s modernization push Delays in the first two phases of the Revised AFP Modernization Program have prompted the Marcos administration to extend funding until 2034, even as the law is set to expire in 2027
Manila in the middle

In the past four years, Marcos has vacillated in his political inclinations, affinity for risk, and even his willingness to engage with the media. But one thing remained: how he frames the Philippines and its place in a region that’s restive at best and volatile at worst.

“The seas around us are arenas of competition and of conflict. Global instability, shifting alliances, and emerging threats demand that we maintain a resilient maritime defense posture,” said Marcos during the Navy’s 128th anniversary last June 9.

Superpower China’s increased willingness to provoke alongside its growing ambitions of dominance in maritime spaces mean that for a country in the literal middle of regional tensions, it’s the Navy’s job to make sure tensions do not rise, even as both deterrence and resilience are in place.
What does resilience mean for the military, exactly?

Marcos’ order as commander-in-chief was for the military, in a worst-case scenario, to be “able to fight and preserve our forces for at least 20 to 30 days” before help from Manila’s friends and allies come, according to then-AFP chief Romeo Brawner Jr. in November 2025.

Thus at peacetime and in the meantime that it is working on manufacturing its own weapons, Manila is seeking to further expand its list of partners it could turn to in both honing its military capacity or in the event of an attack.
The number of military visiting agreements has risen to five from two (a Visiting Forces Agreement with the United States, and a Status of the Visiting Forces Agreement or SOVFA with Australia).

Already signed and concurred with by the Philippine Senate is the Reciprocal Access Agreement with Japan and SOVFAs with New Zealand, Canada, and France. Negotiations for a SOVFA with the United Kingdom are also underway.
Swipe sideways to see the full map.

items: United StatesTreaty allyVisiting forces pactProcurement and aidSole treaty ally. Visiting Forces Agreement. Up to $2.5 billion in foreign military financing, 2026 through 2030.

JapanVisiting forces pactStrategic partnerProcurement and aidReciprocal Access Agreement. Strategic partner. Most of the PCG’s modern vessels, air surveillance radar systems, and refurbished Abukuma-class warships for the Navy.
South KoreaStrategic partnerProcurement and aidStrategic partner. The Navy’s newest frigates and OPVs, and the Air Force’s FA-50s.
VietnamStrategic partnerStrategic partner since before Marcos was elected in 2022.
IndiaStrategic partnerProcurement and aidStrategic partner. The BrahMos coastal defense missile system.
AustraliaVisiting forces pactStrategic partnerStatus of Visiting Forces Agreement. Strategic partner.
New ZealandVisiting forces pactStatus of Visiting Forces Agreement.
FranceVisiting forces pactStatus of Visiting Forces Agreement.
United KingdomVisiting forces pact (in talks)Status of Visiting Forces Agreement under negotiation.
CanadaVisiting forces pactStatus of Visiting Forces Agreement.

blocks.text: Based on the agreements and partnerships cited in this story.

Marcos has also upgraded political ties — to touch on strategic ties, too — with Japan, Vietnam, Australia, South Korea, and India. Before he was elected president in 2022, only Japan and Vietnam were Manila’s strategic partners outside the US. With several of these countries, the Philippines has close ties for defense procurement and aid.

Japan, for example, is the producer of the bulk of the Philippine Coast Guard’s modern vessels, and more are slated for delivery. The PCG is tasked to patrol the Philippines’ maritime spaces to enforce domestic law. Japan is also where the country’s advanced air surveillance radar systems originate, and from whom the Navy will receive refurbished Abukuma-class warships.
From India, the Philippines procured its BrahMos coastal defense missile system. The Navy’s newest frigates and offshore patrol vessels, as well as the Air Force’s FA-50s, are all from South Korea.
The United States, Manila’s sole treaty-ally, has authorized up to $2.5 billion in foreign military financing to the Philippines from 2026 through 2030.

The IISS, in its report, pointed out that the push to manufacture domestically while also forging ties with partners could be a friction point. “Indeed, most stress the importance of partnerships and cooperation, while simultaneously seeking to strengthen domestic industry,” said Béraud-Sudreau. But she pointed this out: “There is a new sense, however, that even the leading defense-industrial powers cannot manufacture the full range of necessary defense capabilities without assistance.”

For Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr., the focus should not just be on sourcing and producing the military’s needs domestically — as the Philippines simply cannot produce all that its military needs.

Supply chain resilience, Teodoro said, is about ensuring foreign sources are reliable, too, even in the face of disruptions. This would mean then, that the Philippines, in procuring defense items, would consider the alignment of either values or strategic goals, too.
For strategists around the world, the key is interdependence.
Manila’s web of friends and partners — a latticework, as some interlocutors put it — can also be a list from which it can pick out trusted sources of new platforms, technologies, and supplies.
But whether that web is managed efficiently or is sustained beyond 2028, when a new administration takes over, is another matter altogether. – Rappler.com

articles.title: US: Man killed in Six Flags roller coaster incident
articles.summary: Local media showed passengers being evacuated from the Goliath coaster, which reaches a maximum height of 61 meters and speeds of up to 113 km/h.

image.caption: People were seein being evacuated from the Goliath roller coasterImage: Emilie Megnien/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: One person has died and several others were injured in an incident on Monday involving a roller coaster at a Six Flags theme park in the United States.
The incident occurred at Six Flags Over Georgia, about 15 miles (24 kilometers) northwest of Atlanta.
Witnesses told local media outlets that they saw a man fall from the ride.
"I cannot imagine the horror the patrons and employees witnessed today, and my heart aches for the family who lost a loved one," said Lisa Cupid, chair of the Cobb County Board of Commissioners.
Six Flags temporary closes 9 roller coasters
Following the incident in Georgia, Six Flags temporarily closed nine roller coasters across six amusement parks.
According to a park spokesperson, similar attractions were closed across their parks "out of an abundance of caution" following the incident at Six Flags Over Georgia.

This comes less than two weeks after Six Flags Magic Mountain in Southern California announced it would retire its famous X2 roller coaster amid lawsuits alleging the ride caused serious brain injuries.
What do we know about the roller coaster?
Althought the park did not identify the ride involved in Monday's incident, local media showed passengers being evacuated from the Goliath coaster.
Built in 2006, Goliath can reach speeds of 113 km/h (70 mph) and a maximum height of 61 meters (200 feet).
According to the theme park's website, riders "navigate through razor-sharp turns and soar over colossal hills."
Monday's death would be at least the seventh to occur at the Georgia theme park, according to the Doan Law Firm, which focuses on amusement park accidents.
That includes one 2006 incident when a man had a likely heart attack while riding the same roller coaster, Goliath.

articles.title: Threat of AI share crash puts world financial stability at risk, says IMF
articles.summary:
High valuations and debt put sector in danger, while fund also warns on government borrowing and cyber-attacks

The threat of an AI share price crash rippling out across global markets is…

blocks.text: The threat of an AI share price crash rippling out across global markets is putting world financial stability at risk, the International Monetary fund has warned.

In its twice-yearly Global Financial Stability Report, the IMF highlighted the sky-high valuations for AI companies along with their increasing debt pile as one reason that risks in the system are “elevated”.

“The consequences of an AI correction could be global,” it warned. Aside from the US, Asian markets would be most exposed, and the UK and euro area potentially more insulated – though their investors with exposure to the US would be hit.
An AI crash was one of three “salient risks” to stability identified by the IMF, alongside rising government borrowing costs and the threat of a big cyber-attack.
It called this trio of factors “plausible near-term catalysts for a sharp tightening of financial conditions and market turmoil”.
The IMF’s analysis underlined the interconnected nature of big AI companies, and the high levels of borrowing being undertaken to fund investment in the sector.

“Weaker or less durable investment and profitability in AI could trigger a correction in AI-related asset prices, exacerbated by rising leverage, concentrated exposures, and circular financing arrangements,” it said.
Such a reassessment would then “sharply reduce investment, trigger equity market corrections, and tighten financial conditions, with global spillovers”.

The “magnificent seven” big tech stocks – Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla – account for more than 35% of the S&P 500 share index in the US, up from 12% a decade ago, and their total market capitalisation has increased by more than 50% in the past two years.

Yet the IMF warned of “growing evidence” that the successful rollout of AI “may not require investment on the massive scale being undertaken by ‘hyperscaler’ firms,” and that “potential economic gains may not be as large as expected”.
The hyperscalers are the companies building the underlying infrastructure for the AI rollout, including many vast datacentres. They include Amazon Web Services, Google, Meta and Oracle.
The IMF also highlighted the growing leverage, or borrowing, that underpins the current boom and could amplify the effects of a crash.
after newsletter promotion
In particular, it identified soaring debts contracted by the companies themselves; hedge fund investment in the sector; and retail investors borrowing to speculate in AI stocks.
In the event of an AI-led market downturn “these growing sources of leverage heighten the potential for forced selling and surges in equity volatility”, it said.

It also pointed to the prevalence of “circular financing” deals, tying stronger AI companies to weaker partners in the same sector, and potentially exacerbating the impact of a share price correction.

It identified $300bn (£227bn) worth of transactions between hyperscalers and “weaker AI firms” in just the past three years, supplemented by $650bn in debt, in exchange for $1.4tn in future financial commitments.

articles.title: Argentina temporarily closes Iguazu Falls after El Niño-fuelled surge in water levels
articles.summary:
National park officials took the precautionary measure to limit tourist access after heavy rain caused the Iguazu River to flow at six times the normal rate

Heavy rainfall fuelled by a

blocks.text: Heavy rainfall fuelled by a supersized El Niño weather pattern briefly forced Argentinian authorities to close tourist access to the famed Iguazu Falls, amid fears that rapidly rising water levels would cause the river to burst its banks.
National park officials took the precautionary measure on Monday when the Iguazu River’s flow exceeded 12,000 cubic metres per second – more than six times its average rate.
It later said the area would reopen to tourists on Tuesday, citing a “gradual decline” in the river’s flow.

José María Hervás, the director of the Iguazu national park, said access was closed because “it just keeps raining” and the volume of water being released from dams upstream on the Iguazu River was not falling, reported the Buenos Aires Times.

blocks.caption: A view of the Iguazu Falls from the Argentinian side of the border.  Photograph: Sinan Dogan/Anadolu/Getty Images

blocks.text: The Iguazu Falls, recognised by Unesco as one of the world’s largest and most impressive waterfalls, sits on the border of Argenina and Brazil and spans approximately 2,700 metres.
In 2023 and 2024, Argentinian officials closed the park on its side of the border over flooding caused by a previous El Niño cycle.

Meteorologists say the 2026-2027 El Niño, which causes global changes in winds and rainfall as well as erratic weather conditions, is certain to be the biggest ever recorded. Scientists now also think human-caused global heating is making El Niño’s more intense.

blocks.caption: Aerial view of Iguazu falls. Photograph: Travel Pix/Alamy

blocks.text: El Niño begins in the equatorial Pacific where changes in winds allow huge amounts of heat to escape the oceans and heat the atmosphere. It grows in the northern hemisphere autumn and peaks in December but has impacts well into the following year.
Last month, Argentina’s coastal region experienced above-average rainfall “similar to that seen during strong El Niño events,” the national meteorological service said.

articles.title: One person dead, several injured in roller-coaster accident near Atlanta
articles.summary: One person has died and several others were injured in an incident involving a Six Flags roller-coaster on Monday afternoon in Georgia, according to police.

image.caption: A roller-coaster is shown at Six Flags Over Georgia on Monday. One person died and several others were injured in an incident involving a roller-coaster at the park. (Emilie Megnien/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New
One person has died and several others were injured in an incident involving a Six Flags roller-coaster on Monday afternoon in Georgia, according to police.
Officials haven't yet given details about what happened on Six Flags Over Georgia ride

Officials did not confirm how the person died or what caused the others to be injured at Six Flags Over Georgia, about 25 kilometres northwest of Atlanta. Detectives with the Cobb County Police Department's major crimes unit are investigating.
A Six Flags spokesperson said the park and local authorities responded immediately and that they are fully co-operating with local authorities as they investigate.
"We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today," the spokesperson said.
Authorities and Six Flags did not identify the roller-coaster. However, local TV stations showed video of passengers being evacuated from the Goliath coaster.
One dead, several injured after incident on a Six Flags roller-coaster in Georgia | Hanomansing Live

The roller-coaster, which was opened in 2006, reaches top speeds of about 113 km/h and heights of 61 metres, the park's website reports. During about 3-1/2 minutes, riders "navigate through razor-sharp turns and soar over colossal hills," according to the website.

"I cannot imagine the horror the patrons and employees witnessed today, and my heart aches for the family who lost a loved one," Lisa Cupid, chair of the Cobb County Board of Commissioners, said in a statement. She added that next of kin have been notified.
The amusement park is a major part of the county's tourism and brings in visitors from across the southeast, Cupid said.
"We are all grappling with how something so devastating could happen at a place that has given generations of families such happy memories," she said.

This death would be at least the seventh at the Georgia park, including one in 2006 in which a man had a likely heart attack on the Goliath coaster, according to the Doan Law Firm, which focuses on amusement park accidents.

It also comes less than two weeks after Six Flags Magic Mountain, in Southern California, announced that it is retiring its famous X2 roller-coaster amid lawsuits alleging serious brain injury caused by the ride. The park had settled one wrongful-death lawsuit from the family of a 22-year-old man who died after riding the coaster in 2022.

Last year, a 32-year-old man died after riding a high-speed roller-coaster at the Universal Epic Universe theme park in Florida. He died from blunt impact injuries, and his death was ruled accidental.
