articles.title: Germany: Labor Minister's resignation puts a spotlight on cracks within the government
articles.summary: Following the sudden resignation of Bärbel Bas as Labor Minister and co-chair of the Social Democratic Party (SPD), accusations are flying in Chancellor Merz's coalition government.

image.caption: Bärbel Bas' resignation sent shockwaves through Germany's governmentImage: Christophe Gateau/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The week kicked off with a bang: On Monday morning, Bärbel Bas announced her resignation as Labor Minister and as Co-Chair of the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD). "Following the death of my stepdaughter, I realized that I need time to come to terms with my grief," Bärbel Bas wrote in a personal statement to party members.

However, she also cited "the public attacks against me — unfortunately, including some from within the ranks of our coalition partner" as reasons for her resignation. In fact, the pressure on Bas increased significantly in recent days. The centrist coalition government is urgently awaiting key legislative proposals from the Ministry of Labor.

Before the summer recess in July,a commission had already presented comprehensive proposals for reforming Germany's statutory pension system. The coalition partners of SPD and the center-right Christian Democratic Union and Christian Social Union (CDU/CSU) wanted these proposals to be quickly turned into legislation. To date, however, no finalized drafts have been presented.
What are the German government's pension, labor reforms?
There had been calls for Bas' resignation

"The minister is no longer tenable. For months, she has been blocking the reforms our country so urgently needs," railed Christian von Stetten, head of the CDU/CSU parliamentary group's caucus representing medium-sized enterprises, said in reference to Bas in September.

In early October, such criticism was echoed by CDU Economy Minister Katherina Reiche, who demanded that the pension reform be passed by the end of the year. Bas had to submit the bill "promptly," Reiche said, although it was known at the time what a difficult personal situation her cabinet colleague was in at the time.

SPD co-leader, Finance Minister and Vice-Chancellor Lars Klingbeil reacted sharply on Monday, saying the political attacks against Bas had been "disgraceful." Following a meeting of the SPD leadership, he told journalists in Berlin: "This poisons the political discourse, and — in the interest of preserving our political culture — I hope that everyone will take a step back and reflect on what has actually happened over the past few weeks." He called on all centrist politicians to be careful "that we don't destroy the good people in politics by attacking one another."
Such accusations carry significant weight at a time when the coalition is already mired in a deep crisis.

Adding to this is the new vacancy at the top of the SPD. Without Bas, Klingbeil will lead the SPD alone. A party convention will be scheduled for December or January to elect new leadership for the Social Democrats. It is not certain whether Klingbeil will run again. He had received a very poor result during his last reelection as party leader.
What's behind the rising polarization in German politics?
Swift replacement of Labor Minister

Alexander Schweitzer is to succeed Bärbel Bas as Federal Minister of Labor. The former state premier of the state of Rhineland-Palatinate had previously served as that state's Minister of Labor and Social Affairs. Chancellor Friedrich Merz expressed confidence that Schweitzer's experience would ensure " good cooperation within the federal government," adding that he hoped that the pending legislative proposals "will now be quickly approved by the cabinet and can be introduced into the parliamentary process."

The chancellor refuted the accusations leveled by Bas, saying that he had never discussed personal matters with her. Friedrich Merz said he had explicitly advised Bas to take the time she needed to grieve.
Merz promises change
Mistrust between the coalition partners has increased significantly, with SPD lawmakers speaking of an increasingly toxic political climate.

For months, the CDU and SPD have been grappling with low poll numbers, disappointing election results, and disputes over key reform projects. Plans for changes to the electricity tax, the introduction of a sugar tax, the pension and the labor market reform — hardly any initiative has been able to proceed without public controversy.

Adding to this is the crisis within the chancellor's party, the CDU, which saw a historic election defeat in the eastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania in September, when it even lost representation in a state parliament for the first time in history.
On Sunday and Monday morning, therefore, the party leadership met for a closed-door session to discuss the way forward.

They produced a four-page document which indicates a shift in priorities, to put more emphasis on social issues: Affordable housing, lower electricity prices, better health care, and greater respect for citizens' lifetime achievements are mentioned in the paper. This is seen as a response to criticism that the CDU had been focusing too much on economic and regulatory issues.
Why Germany's political center is losing ground

The chancellor admitted that voters feel that politicians are not taking their hardships and fears of social decline seriously enough. "We have to work our way out of this slump — and get out of a crisis of confidence," Merz said. "You can't just reinvent a party overnight over a weekend, but we want to show that we're ready for change," the chancellor said, adding: "and we have to be, given the election results."
The chancellor announced that he would lower the electricity tax for everyone — a promise he had made before the general election in 2025 but had not kept.

With the closed-door meeting paper, the CDU is also sending a notable signal to the SPD. Instead of a programmatic shift further to the right, it is emphasizing its traditional social values — a stance that resonates well within the Social Democratic Party.

The chancellor made an effort to emphasize his intention to continue with the current coalition government: "The personnel changes will not call into question the basis of the coalition agreement," Merz said. He then repeated what he had recently said during a visit to Ukraine: "We need a stable federal government right now in order to remain capable of acting on the international stage."

Both CDU/CSU and SPD know that calling early elections could primarily benefit the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), which is leading in the polls nationwide. So despite the deep rifts, Lars Klingbeil and Friedrich Merz currently see no alternative to their coalition.
This article was originally published in German.

articles.title: Canada, U.K. allies vow action after RAF Fairford terror plot
articles.summary: Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand joined her counterparts in 28 other countries in a statement condemning Iran's attacks against them and vowing to take action against anyone acting on behalf of…

image.caption: Foreign Minister Anita Anand, seen at the United Nations headquarters in New York City last month, joined nearly 30 other foreign ministers in condemning Iran for its alleged involvement in a series of attacks on European soil. (Eduardo Munoz/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand joined her counterparts in 28 other countries in a statement condemning Iran's attacks against them and vowing to take action against anyone acting on behalf of Tehran. The statement comes after the U.K. cited Iran's involvement in a suspected plot targeting the RAF Fairford airbase in Britain.
U.S., U.K. and other allies condemn Iran's attacks against them, vow to take action against proxies

The alleged terror plot was foiled Sept. 27 when police arrested five London-based men on suspicion of explosive and terrorism offenses after a tip-off that three vans had been heading to the military airfield, which has been used to strike Iran.

The statement released Monday said the U.K. had concluded the incident demonstrates the Iranian regime's "continued willingness to project hostile activity beyond its borders through covert networks and proxy actors" and comes after a recent string of attacks across Europe targeting Jewish communities, U.S. interests and Iranian journalists.

items: U.K. police arrest 5 near airbase used by U.S. on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act
British police release 5 London-based men after arrests near airbase used by U.S.

blocks.text: Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (HAYI), a group tied to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), claimed responsibility for that string of attacks.
"Any attempt by Iran to threaten, silence, intimidate, harass, harm, or coerce people on our territories through proxies or any other means is unacceptable," the statement reads.

It is signed by the foreign ministers of Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, the United Kingdom and the United States.
"Iran should be in no doubt that we are united and remain committed to safeguarding our sovereignty and strengthening our international coordination," the statement also said.

The RAF Fairford airbase in Fairford, England, is seen last week after police declared a major incident there and arrested several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act. The men have since been released on bail. (Toby Shepheard/Reuters)
U.K.'s Burnham says plot 'likely' co-ordinated by Iran

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday that a suspected plot targeting the RAF Fairford airbase in Britain was "highly likely" to have been co-ordinated in Iran, and almost certainly directed by the IRGC.
"I can confirm our assessment that it is highly likely to have been co-ordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard," Burnham told Parliament.

Tehran has rejected any suggestion it was involved in the Fairford incident, saying it amounted to "unfounded and malicious ​speculations." Iran's ambassador to the U.K., Seyed Ali Masouvi, denied any Iranian role in the suspected RAF Fairford plot, according to Iran's state news agency.

Details around the suspected plot remain thin. The five detained men were later released without charge on ‌police ⁠bail "under stringent conditions," and two other arrested men, including a British-Iranian national, have also been released.
Detectives have said petrol but no viable explosive had been found in vans seized along with the five men. However, both police and Burnham have pointed toward the involvement of a foreign state.

"We will not tolerate these threats on our soil," Burnham said. "We will crack down on Iran's use of criminal networks, using our full range of powers to target them and their funding streams, and we will bring further sanctions to restrict the capacity of Iran and the IRGC to do us harm."

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, seen at an event in Manchester, England, last week, told U.K. Parliament Monday the suspected plot against RAF Fairford was likely co-ordinated by Iran. (Christopher Furlong/Reuters)
British Foreign Minister Ed Miliband said he had summoned the Iranian ambassador while the ministry announced two Iranian nationals had been sanctioned.

The two men were Ruhollah Bazghandi, who Britain said was the IRGC's head of counterespionage operations, and Shahram Ali Reza Tamarzadeh Jakki, a facilitator for the already sanctioned Zindashti criminal network, which is accused of involvement in several plots against Iranian dissidents.
With files from Reuters

articles.title: Democrats condemn 'deeply disturbing' raid on Rep. Ilhan Omar's home ahead of U.S. midterms
articles.summary: Democratic leaders in the U.S. House of Representatives have condemned a raid on the home of Rep. Ilhan Omar, a Minnesota congresswoman and frequent target of U.S. President Donald Trump's personal…

image.caption: Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., stands during a news conference on Jan. 28 in Minneapolis. U.S. federal agents searched Omar's home on Monday as part of a criminal investigation, according to media reports. (Adam Gray/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

Democratic leaders in the U.S. House of Representatives have condemned a raid on the home of Rep. Ilhan Omar, a Minnesota congresswoman and frequent target of U.S. President Donald Trump's personal attacks. The raid comes just weeks ahead of U.S. midterm elections.
U.S. federal agents searched Omar's home Monday, according to multiple media reports
· CBC News
· Posted: Oct 12, 2026 1:02 PM EDT | Last Updated: 11 minutes ago

Democratic leaders in the U.S. House of Representatives have condemned a raid on Rep. Ilhan Omar's home as "deeply disturbing" and accused the Trump administration of a "rogue abuse of power" just weeks ahead of November's midterm elections.
U.S. federal agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar's home earlier on Monday as part of a criminal investigation, The Associated Press and other U.S. media outlets reported, citing unnamed sources.

Citing two sources familiar with the matter who spoke on condition of anonymity, AP said Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents carried out the search of Omar's home. But the news agency said the nature and the scope of the investigation were unclear.

In a written statement later on Monday, Democratic House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said U.S. President Donald Trump had targeted Omar — a Minnesota congresswoman and the first Somali-American lawmaker in Congress — with "vile personal attacks" for years.
"Now, less than 30 days until the midterm election, his violent mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family," reads the statement.
Department of Homeland Security officers carry boxes from the Washington, D.C., residence of Rep. Ilhan Omar on Monday. (J. Scott Applewhite/The Associated Press)
It was also signed by House minority whip Rep. Katherine Clark and Rep. Pete Aguilar, chair of the House Democratic Caucus.
"The American people deserve transparency, and we will deliver full accountability for the rogue abuse of power from the Department of Homeland Security and Department of Justice," they said.
Federal criminal investigation
In a written statement to CBC News, the Justice Department said HSI agents "executed a judicially authorized search warrant" in the Washington, D.C., area, which had been secured by the department.
"This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation," it said.

U.S. Vice-President JD Vance has accused Omar of committing immigration fraud, without providing details, and has said that he and deputy White House chief of staff Stephen Miller were trying to figure out how to investigate the congresswoman.

items: What questions do you have about the US Midterm elections?
How the ICE surge in Minnesota could impact the midterms

blocks.text: Omar has broadly denied the allegations as "disgusting lies." Her office in March dismissed Vance's claims as fabricated and defamatory.
DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said last month that there was an "ongoing investigation" and "something's going to happen," AP reported.
Omar responded to Monday's raid on social media, saying it was "an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement."
"For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced," she wrote on X.
Jacklyn Rogers, a spokesperson for Omar, also said in an email to CBC that "the Congresswoman has done nothing wrong."
Target of Trump's attacks
Omar has been a frequent target of attacks by Trump and members of his Republican Party.

In February, Trump said Omar and fellow progressive Democrat, Rep. Rashida Tlaib, "should be institutionalized" and sent "back from where they came" after they shouted at him during his State of the Union address.
‘You killed Americans!’: Ilhan Omar shouts at Trump during speech

The Republican leader, who has carried out an immigration crackdown since he returned to the White House in early 2025, also has described Somali immigrants as "garbage" and said, "we don't want them in our country."
In a social media post last week, Trump said "the once Great State of Minnesota is being taken over by Somali Immigrants."
Omar, a staunch critic of Trump's immigration policies, condemned the comments. "Trump's obsession with demonizing the Somali community is dangerous and reprehensible," she wrote on X.
Midterm elections loom
Monday's raid comes just weeks before the U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3, with Republicans trying to retain slim control of the House of Representatives and the Senate.
Omar, who is running for re-election, represents a safe Democratic district where she won re-election in 2024 by a margin of 50 percentage points.
Justice Department policy bars federal prosecutors and agents from timing any action to affect the ‌outcome of any election or benefiting a candidate or political party.

items: Why Minneapolis has become such a flashpoint amid ICE deployments
Somali communities say ‘people feel insecure and live in fear’ after Trump's tirade

blocks.text: The department has historically avoided taking investigative steps against political candidates within about 60 days of an election.

Several Democrats spoke out in defence of Omar on Monday, with Rep. Delia Ramirez of Illinois calling the raid "an absolute abuse of power" and California Gov. Gavin Newsom, another fierce Trump critic, describing it as "straight out of the authoritarian playbook."
Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz also said on social media: "Americans see this for what it is — President Trump is abusing his power to go after political opponents weeks before an election."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Jillian Kestler-D'Amours is a senior writer at CBC based in Montreal. You can reach her at jillian.kestler-d.amours@cbc.ca.
With files from The Associated Press and Reuters

articles.title: Sara Duterte impeachment trial Day 38: VP dropped as witness; P1.5B 'unexplained wealth'
articles.summary: Prosecution witness and Atty. Alex Cabrera marked the last day of the prosecution"s presentation of evidence by testifying that the unexplained wealth of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband,…

blocks.text: Published October 13, 2026 1:01am

Prosecution witness and Atty. Alex Cabrera marked the last day of the prosecution’s presentation of evidence by testifying that the unexplained wealth of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, could reach as much as P1.5 billion.

Cabrera also said that the financial records of the Duterte-Carpio couple showed "symptoms of money laundering," citing P41 million and P55 million unused manager's checks under the joint account of the Vice President and her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte.
The unused manager's checks were eventually used as a payout to Mr. Duterte (P41 million) and businessman Sammy Uy (P16 million).

These amounts are on top of the P41 million over-the-counter withdrawal that Carpio made last August 6, 2024. This happened days after Sara Duterte quit as DepEd Secretary and a complaint was filed against Carpio in connection with his alleged involvement in the magnetic lifter that carried P6.4 billion worth of illegal drugs.
Senator-judge Joel Villanueva flagged the 2025 sale of stocks of Cale88 Foods Corporation, a declared asset of Carpio, to a certain firm that had only P84,000 worth of assets.

Defense lawyer Kristine Ferrer also explained that the hundreds of thousands of pesos spent on food and shoes made by Carpio in Japan and in Davao, were for groups of people and for their son's basketball team.

Cabrera also said that his forensic investigation on the financial records of the Vice President and her husband is based on the official government records provided by the prosecution. He added he did not have any document analyzed that was provided by the Vice President.
Defense team lead counsel Sheila Sison said Cabrera’s testimony should not be given weight since they were mere “unbridled and erroneous conclusions of law and fact.”
House prosecutor Chel Diokno of Akbayan party-list moved to strike Sison’s remarks off the record for being an irresponsible statement, if not “totally out of place and has no meaning.”
Escudero ruled that both Sison's and Diokno's remarks will remain on the record.
Before Sison, defense counsel Ferrer also asked Cabrera whether he was bothered by the punitive confidentiality clause of the Anti-Money Laundering Law.

Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo asked the prosecution panel to check whether the subject properties of the Duterte-Carpio couple as announced by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) are part of the undeclared assets of the Vice President and her husband.
As Cabrera wrapped up his testimony, the prosecution also decided not to field Sara Duterte as a hostile witness anymore.

Private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan said that given that previous hostile witnesses from the Office of the Vice President merely said they don’t know or are unaware of the allegations, it is likely that the Vice President will resort to the same tactic.
Meanwhile, the House prosecution panel remained unfazed amid the latest Pulse Asia poll survey showing Sara Duterte leading by a mile over her potential rivals in the 2028 presidential elections.

“Assuming that the results are accurate and people trust her, all the more that she should be held accountable, and that is through evidence," private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa, Jr. said in a press conference. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: LOOK: Palace's farewell call for outgoing Spanish Ambassador Miguel Utray

A farewell call was held for outgoing Spanish Ambassador to the Philippines Miguel Utray at the Study Room in Malacañan Palace.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. received Utray and extended his gratitude for “strengthening the cooperation between the Philippines and Spain” during his four-year duty in the country, the Presidential Communications Office (PCO) said.
Utray assumed the post in October 2022. He is scheduled to depart Manila on October 14, 2026, to take up his new assignment as Spain’s Ambassador to Angola.
The PCO recounted key milestones during his tenure, including the Philippines and Spain’s bilateral trade reaching US$ 1.073 billion in 2025, up from US$ 994.25 million in 2024.

“Spain ranked as the Philippines’ 24th largest trading partner in 2024, with major Philippine exports including tuna, skipjack, bonito, coconut oil, pineapples, and other agricultural and manufactured products,” the PCO said.

“Tourism exchanges also recorded significant growth during Ambassador Utray’s posting, with visitor arrivals from Spain nearly doubling to 60,290 in 2025 from 30,581 in 2024. Meanwhile, Filipino tourists visiting Spain reached 185,000 arrivals in 2025, up from 125,000 the year before,” it added, citing Utray.
Diplomatic relations between the Philippines and Spain were formally established in 1947 and will mark their 80th anniversary in 2027.
According to PCO, approximately 51,855 Filipinos are employed in the services sector in Spain, based on the latest data. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Six Ukrainian energy sites hit by Russia since Trump announced ceasefire, Zelensky says
articles.summary: Despite the US president announcing energy infrastructure would not be targeted strikes have continued, Ukraine says.

blocks.text: Image source, EPA
Emergency services responded to a Russian drone strike on a residential building in Kharkiv, north-eastern Ukraine on Monday
ByOlivia Ireland and Ella Kipling
Russia struck six Ukrainian energy facilities hours after US President Donald Trump announced the two countries had agreed to an energy ceasefire, Volodymyr Zelensky has said.
Despite Trump stating on Sunday the truce would be "effective immediately", the Ukrainian president said Russia had hit "our gas stations, energy infrastructure, and other facilities".

There were blackouts in the city of Izyum after a Russian strike destroyed power grids, Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform said, while energy and railway infrastructure in western Ukraine was also targeted overnight.
On Monday, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Ukraine does not deserve the "respite" a ceasefire would bring.
Zelensky said 33 people had been injured in the strikes on energy facilities across the country.
He told Fox News: "We did not attack, while Russia attacked our gas stations, energy infrastructure, and other facilities."
"I think it was Putin's answer to President Trump," he added.
Global conflicts have pushed fuel prices higher ahead of the US midterm elections and on Friday Trump announced a plan to import Russian diesel into the US on Friday.
On Monday, Ukraine's state-owned grid operator Ukrenergo reported "new power cuts" in Kharkiv, Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia due to damage caused to energy equipment by Russian attacks.
Electricity rationing has been introduced in parts of Ukraine to avoid overloading damaged equipment, Ukrenergo said.
Zelensky said on X the strikes were proof Russia was "unwilling to accept an energy ceasefire".
On Monday evening, Kyiv's mayor Vitali Klitschko posted on Telegram that a drone hit a 25-story residential building in the Darnytskyi district.
Several cars in the building's courtyard were also on fire, he said, but it is not clear how many casualties there may be.
Watch: What could Trump's energy ceasefire claim mean for Ukraine?

When Trump first announced the ceasefire on Sunday, Zelensky said it was "news to him" that a truce was in effect, but he backed the proposed ceasefire as a "major step toward ending the war, if the Americans truly step in now and make sure Russians respect the energy ceasefire".
For months, Ukraine and Russia have been exchanging strikes on energy infrastructure, disrupting energy supplies on both sides.

Moscow has said the installations it hits are legitimate targets as they support Ukraine's military operation, while Zelensky has characterised Ukrainian attacks deep inside Russian territory as part of an effort to "reduce Russia's ability to finance the war".
Analysis by BBC Verify on both Ukrainian and Russian strikes during the war have found both sides have increased their attacks in the lead up to the next winter.
In 2026, BBC Verify has recorded 273 strikes on Russian-controlled oil and gas facilities, more than double the 124 recorded over the same period in 2025.

Separately, analysis of data aggregated by global conflict monitor, the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data project (Acled), recorded 2.4 times as many reported Russian attacks affecting Ukraine's energy network so far this year.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Energy facilities in Kharkiv were hit by Russian strikes on Sunday evening, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said

blocks.text: Image source, EPA/Shutterstock
Energy facilities in Kharkiv were hit by Russian strikes on Sunday evening, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said
Trump has been urging Ukraine to stop strikes on Russian oil infrastructure, so Russia can fulfil the recently struck deal to release diesel to the US and the global market.
The deal temporarily undoes US sanctions on energy imports, which Zelensky described as a "gift" to Russian President Vladimir Putin.
What's behind Trump's energy ceasefire claim?
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Britain "strongly supports President Trump's call today for a sustained energy ceasefire to start now", while France, Canada and the EU also expressed support.
However, there has been a mixed response among European officials.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the bloc would welcome an energy ceasefire "when it holds". Kallas said at a meeting of EU foreign ministers on Monday: "We haven't yet seen that also Russia will stick to it."
Meanwhile, Estonia's foreign minister said the ceasefire was "not working".
Additional reporting by Benedict Garman, BBC Verify

articles.title: ICC Prosecution restructures evidence list vs. Rodrigo Duterte, seeks admission of 3 recorded testimonies
articles.summary: The International Criminal Court (ICC) Office of the Prosecutor has restructured its List of Evidence in former President Rodrigo Duterte"s case, following a further review of the materials.
articles.byline: Jay-vee Marasigan Pangan, Andy Peñafuerte III

blocks.text: Published October 13, 2026 12:42am
The International Criminal Court (ICC) Office of the Prosecutor has restructured its List of Evidence in former President Rodrigo Duterte’s case, following a further review of the materials.

In a filing made public on October 12, Acting Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang said the revised list was divided into seven categories “in order to provide a clearer understanding of the categories of evidence the Prosecution seeks to rely upon.”
The prosecution also said it had further reviewed the list following the September status conference and removed 253 items, so far.
The seven categories include:

items: Materials cited in the prosecution’s Trial Brief and annexes;
Materials related to trial witnesses;
Speeches by Duterte and other alleged co-perpetrators;
Several datasets;
Materials received from a redacted source and non-governmental organizations;
Open-source material; and
Other evidence

blocks.text: One of the datasets is publicly described as containing Philippine National Police (PNP) “records related to killings in PNP anti-drug operations and other drug-related killings during the charged period.” Some dataset names and sources of material remain redacted in the public filing.
The prosecution said materials cited in its Trial Brief and annexes comprise the “key items of evidence” in its case.

The prosecution also said it could remove almost 7,000 more items “should the Defence agree to the proposed agreed facts in relation to the [REDACTED] collection.” The filing does not publicly identify that collection.
The filing comes amid continuing disputes over the volume and organization of evidence in Duterte’s case.

During the September status conference, Duterte’s defense raised concerns about the amount of material it had to review ahead of trial. Meanwhile, the prosecution has maintained that it has taken steps to organize and disclose the evidence.
Disclosure and the prosecution’s List of Evidence are also among the matters expected to be discussed during Duterte’s fourth status conference on October 13.
Prosecution seeks to use recorded testimony of three witnesses
In another filing also made public on October 12, Niang asked Trial Chamber III to admit the prior recorded testimonies of three witnesses instead of requiring them to testify live.

Niang said the testimonies of witnesses identified as P-1370, P-1393 and P-1416 are “viva voce” (oral rather than written) and mainly concern alleged extrajudicial killings in Central Luzon and the “contextual elements of crimes against humanity.”
“All Three Witnesses have attested that their Prior Recorded Testimonies were given voluntarily and their contents were true to the best of their recollection of the events,” the filing stated.
“The Prior Recorded Testimonies that the Prosecution seeks to introduce into evidence, pursuant to rule 68(2)(b) of the Rules, are relevant, reliable and probative.”
Niang said the accounts relate to an alleged policy to “neutralise” suspected criminals through violent crimes, including murder.”

One of the witnesses, P-1393, allegedly described a killing involving police officers in San Jose del Monte, Bulacan. According to the prosecution filing, the witnesses said officers manufactured a self-defense scenario and planted drugs, a gun, and money on the victim.

The same witness also described a change in police conduct during “One Time Big Time” (OTBT) operations after Duterte became president, including what the prosecution characterized as a “preference for killings instead of arrests.”
The prosecution argued that using the recorded statement would save court time and resources and would not prejudice Duterte’s rights.

It also stated that the defense could cross-examine viva voce witnesses “on the basis of information contained in the Prior Recorded Testimonies”, argue on the weight of these testimonies “to the extent that discrepancies exist with other evidence”, or present contradictory evidence.

“Granting the request will enhance the expeditiousness of the proceedings, obviate the unnecessary appearance of the witnesses, save valuable court time and resources, and serve the interests of justice,” the prosecution said.
ICC Trial Chamber III will convene the fourth status conference for Duterte’s case tomorrow, October 13. The chamber expects Duterte to appear before the court.
The trial for the former president’s case of crimes against humanity is scheduled for November 30. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Ex-political prisoners ask Ombudsman to reconsider complaints vs. PNP officials
articles.summary: Two former political prisoners asked the Office of the Ombudsman to reconsider the complaints filed against several PNP officers over alleged illegal detention and planting of evidence.

Two former political prisoners on Monday asked the Office of the Ombudsman to reconsider the complaints filed against several Philippine National Police (PNP) officers over alleged illegal detention and planting of evidence.

According to Katribu Kalipunan ng Katutubong Mamamayan ng Pilipinas, Manobo tribe member Julieta Gomez and indigenous people’s rights advocate Niezel Velasco were detained for four years and were released in April 2025 after the court junked the cases against them.

Gomez and Velasco filed a countercharge against five PNP officers for false testimony against a defendant, false testimony in other cases and perjury in solemn affirmation, unlawful arrest, liability for planting of evidence, and administrative charges.
“Ang ganitong kalakaran ay nagpapakita kung paanong madaling baluktutin ang rule of law upang pagtakpan ang mga paglabag ng estado at ng mga galamay nito,” the group said in a statement.
(This kind of practice shows how easily the rule of law can be distorted to cover up the violations of the state and its minions.)
“Ang tunay na hustisya ay makakamtan lamang kung papanagutin ang mga pulis na sangkot at kung titigil ang sistematikong pang-aabuso ng estado,” it added.
(Ang tunay na hustisya ay makakamtan lamang kung papanagutin ang mga pulis na sangkot at kung titigil ang sistematikong pang-aabuso ng estado.)

articles.title: 'More men need to be standing up': Dan Levy calls out Shane Gillis monologue about women's clothing
articles.summary: Comedian Shane Gillis joked in his opening SNL monologue on Saturday about the length of some women's shorts at the gym, referring to them with an offensive term. The comments prompted backlash from…

image.caption: Producer and actor Dan Levy, seen at the Toronto International Film Festival in 2025, took to Instagram to criticize comedian Shane Gillis's joke about the length of women's shorts at the gym and the offensive word used to describe those who wear them. (Sammy Kogan/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

Comedian Shane Gillis joked in his opening SNL monologue on Saturday about the length of some women's shorts at the gym, referring to them with an offensive term. The comments prompted backlash from Levy and regular SNL fans alike, who called the joke misogynistic.
Gillis, who was fired from SNL in 2019 shortly after being brought on, is no stranger to controversy
Warning: This article contains offensive language.
Dan Levy isn't laughing at Shane Gillis's Saturday Night Live monologue — and he's not happy with men who find it funny, either.

In a Sunday Instagram video, Levy didn't mention Gillis by name, but called out the reference to women who wear short shorts to the gym as "whores," which Gillis made the night before in an introductory segment while hosting the long-running sketch comedy show.
"I haven't been to the gym in so long, I didn't know women just dress like whores now," Gillis said. "I'm sorry, there's no other way to describe [it]."
Gillis critiqued the neon short-shorts that he says he sees women wear at the gym, comparing the attire to the "artificial bait" of a fishing lure.
"And don't look; you're not allowed to look," Gillis added.
Gillis, seen hosting the ESPY Awards in Los Angeles in 2025, drew criticism over the weekend for a joke included in his SNL monologue. (Mark J. Terrill/Associated Press)
In response, Levy took to Instagram to voice his anger with the comments, saying he was "speechless" a joke of that nature would be broadcast on live television.

"Women wearing short shorts at the gym doesn't make them whores," Levy, star of Schitt's Creek who hosted SNL himself in 2021, said in an Instagram video. "It makes the men calling them whores misogynists."
"And to be perfectly honest, more men need to be standing up in opposition to it because it's complacency that has created the environment [in] which women are sexually assaulted," Levy went on.

The Canadian-born comedian added that the objectification of women in the media by men will lead other men to "treat them like objects," and he said that everyone should be standing up for women in order to prevent their mistreatment.

The backlash to Gillis's comments comes amid a wave of outrage against the men who've become known as the Cornell 7, who are accused of a 2024 gang rape at an Ivy League frat house, and support for their accuser known only as Jane Doe. The case has ignited scrutiny over the school's handling of the situation as well as conversations about consent and the culture that would have allowed the situation to happen in the first place.

items: What to know about Cornell's alleged frat house gang-rape case and the 'Cornell 7'

blocks.text: Plenty of SNL fans also criticized the joke and those on the show who approved it, especially given the ongoing conversation around the alleged rape at Cornell.
"Who on earth approved the "wh*res" joke?! Read the room," one commenter said on the video of Gillis's monologue posted to the SNL Instagram account.
"Shane is very aware of the current moment with Jane Doe. And he chose that joke anyways," another wrote.

Others commented under Gillis's most recent, unrelated Instagram post, saying the monologue was misogynistic and enabled rape culture. Some fans came to his defence, saying the comedian should be able to make the jokes.
Students march at UBC in support of alleged Cornell University gang-rape victim

Gillis is no stranger to controversy, including on the SNL stage. In 2019, the comedian was hired and then quickly dropped as a cast member on the show after podcast clips of Gillis making homophobic jokes and using an Asian slur circulated.

He's since hosted the show on three occasions, however — in 2024, 2025 and again last Saturday. During his first SNL appearance, Gillis joked about a family member of his with Down syndrome, and he has been criticized for his use of homophobic language on podcasts.
LISTEN | In 'Tires', is Shane Gillis making fun of his character, or just being himself?:
Commotion with Elamin Abdelmahmoud15:33What do we do with Tires?

The comments about women's appearances at the gym weren't the only ones to raise eyebrows this Saturday, either. He also said he'd "balded directly into an Adolf Hitler haircut" that he struggles to adjust without looking "gay."
"You're either gay or you're Hitler. Isn't that where we're at as a country," he quipped.

In a later sketch parodying a Dr. Seuss story, Gillis accidentally dropped the f-word — a no-go on the live program, which let the word go out to viewers in some time zones uncensored. Gillis apologized for cursing twice, once at the end of the sketch and during the show's goodbye.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Abby Hughes is a writer with CBC News based in Toronto. Originally from Orillia, Ont., she studied journalism at Toronto Metropolitan University. She covers news from the worlds of business, entertainment, health, science and education, and her favourite stories focus on the real people in those areas — the customers, fans, patients, citizens and students. You can reach her with story ideas at abby.hughes@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Sara: Marcos sees me as threat since 2023
articles.summary: Instead of explaining her alleged ties to Chinese money, Vice President Sara Duterte claimed she was being targeted by the administration, and has been considered a “threat” by President…

blocks.text: October 13, 2026 | 12:00am
Vice President Sara Duterte and President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — Instead of explaining her alleged ties to Chinese money, Vice President Sara Duterte claimed she was being targeted by the administration, and has been considered a “threat” by President Marcos since 2023.
Marcos over the weekend said it could be a national security threat “at the highest level” if the company linked to Duterte and her husband Manases Carpio indeed received funds from China.

“It’s worrying that such a statement would come from (Bongbong Marcos) because it seems like he has admitted that since 2023 they have considered me a threat. This is worrying because he is saying that the Vice President is a threat to the country,” Duterte said at a press conference yesterday.
She added that Marcos’ statement has serious implications on her security and the security of the Philippines.

Marcos has ordered an investigation after an Anti-Money Laundering Council report exposed remittances from China to Cale88 Foods Corp., a firm linked to Carpio, who held a substantial 47.5 percent stake.

“Marcos‘ statement clearly states that for him, doing business with China is a threat to the security of the Philippines. This carries the connotation of a warning to Filipino businessmen doing business in China,” she said.

“And above all, the statement explicitly accuses China of interfering in the internal affairs of the Philippines. Although it lacks sufficient justification, it is a bold and dangerous challenge to China – a country with a long history of relations with the Philippines. This is serious. And it could have a serious impact on our relationship with China,” she added.

Duterte and members of her family, including detained former president Rodrigo Duterte, have always been perceived to be soft on China, particularly on the territorial dispute in the West Philippine Sea.

articles.title: Philippines eyes ‘green revolution’
articles.summary: The Marcos administration will embark on a campaign to encourage the public to reuse water and revive a “green revolution” to ease the impact of a “super El Niño.”

blocks.text: October 13, 2026 | 12:00am
Stock image of running water from faucet.
SINGAPORE – The Marcos administration will embark on a campaign to encourage the public to reuse water and revive a “green revolution” to ease the impact of a “super El Niño.”
In a media interview on Sunday here, Marcos cited the need to think about ways to collect every drop of water from dams and households and explain to Filipinos the climate phenomenon.
“Part of that public service and those public service messages will be collect, buy buckets so that when it rains, you can collect everything,” Marcos said.

“We will teach you... We will give you the filter. We’ll teach you how to do everything so you will not get sick and you will treat water properly. And it will be healthy even for little children. So that’s water supply,” he added.
Vice President Sara Duterte said, “We can no longer expect anything from the President. I will not comment on his buckets.”
An El Niño information campaign is being prepared by the Office of the Vice President.
El Niño is projected to intensify in the coming months and persist through the first half of 2027.
‘Plantita’ revival
Marcos is pushing for a “green revolution” to ensure enough vegetable supply, which is expected to be hit hard by the dry spell due to potential water supply issues.

“Let us go back to the green revolution. Let’s encourage everybody. We had a green revolution before, a long time ago. Then, during the pandemic, the ‘plantita’ was revived. Let us continue that,” he said, referring to Filipinos who made planting a hobby during the lockdown.
“Let’s just keep that going. Get everybody to plant their own vegetables... It won’t solve the entire problem, but it will help,” he asserted.
In 1973, the late president Ferdinand Marcos Sr. launched a “green revolution” to boost food supply and nutrition efforts.
The project encouraged backyard planting of vegetables and fruits. — Bella Cariaso

articles.title: Sara, Bong Go top choices for president, VP – Pulse
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte and Sen. Bong Go remained the most preferred candidates for president and vice president, respectively, according to a recent survey conducted by Pulse Asia.

blocks.text: October 13, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte and Sen. Bong Go remained the most preferred candidates for president and vice president, respectively, according to a recent survey conducted by Pulse Asia.
Results of the Sept. 17 to 24 survey released yesterday showed 50 percent of the respondents saying they would vote for Duterte for president if the 2028 elections were held during the survey period.
She led by a 24-point margin against Naga City Mayor and former vice president Leni Robredo, who placed second with the support of 26 percent of the respondents.

Following them were Sen. Raffy Tulfo with 12 percent, Sen. Risa Hontiveros with three percent, Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro with one percent, Public Works and Highways Secretary Vince Dizon with one percent and Baguio City Mayor Benjie Magalong with 0.3 percent.
Seven percent of the respondents did not support a specific individual.
For the vice presidential race, Go was still the most preferred candidate with the support of 31 percent of the respondents.

He was followed by Sen. Robin Padilla with 19 percent, Sen. Bam Aquino with 17 percent, former senator Grace Poe with 14 percent, Sen. Erwin Tulfo with 10 percent, Sen. Francis Pangilinan with three percent and Metropolitan Manila Development Authority general manager Nic Torre with 0.3 percent. Five percent did not support any particular candidate for vice president.
The survey was conducted amid the ongoing impeachment trial of the Vice President. Only Duterte has publicly declared her intention to run for higher office in 2028.
Among possible candidates for Senate in 2028, Poe emerged as the most preferred candidate with the support of 50.2 percent.

Following her were Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano (46.5 percent), Sen. Robin Padilla (45.9 percent), Sen. Raffy Tulfo (44.4 percent), Davao City Mayor Baste Duterte (37.2 percent), former senator Manny Pacquiao (36.5 percent), Sen. Loren Legarda (33 percent).

Also on top of the list were former senator and incumbent Makati Mayor Nancy Binay (31.7 percent), Sen. Francis Escudero (30.1 percent), former senator and incumbent Education Secretary Sonny Angara (26.3 percent), broadcaster Ben Tulfo (86 percent) and Tourism Infrastructure and Enterprise Zone Authority chief operating officer Mark Lapid (19.8 percent).
Outside the so-called “Magic 12” but within statistical chances of winning were Sen. Jinggoy Estrada, television host Willie Revillame and detained former congressman Mike Defensor.
The survey had 2,400 respondents and a margin of error of plus/minus two percent.
‘No-election scenario’
Duterte, meanwhile, has warned anew of “no-election” scenario in 2028, citing efforts to stop her, particularly through impeachment.
“First is impeachment. Second, there is Charter change. And third, no-elections. So, I’ve been warning you for a long time,” Duterte said at a press conference.
Duterte’s known ally Sen. Imee Marcos also warned of a “no-election” scenario in 2028, citing the postponement of the 2026 Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections to November 2028.

“You know, I just noticed that they were trying to link all the illegal activities with me… confidential funds, corruption. Actually, there’s more. They are trying to link us with drugs. So corruption, drugs. Now they have China funds,” Duterte noted.
Duterte accused the administration of trying everything to stop her in her presidential bid.

“The narrative changed. Now, we have shifted to China and become a national security risk for businesses that trade with China… They will do everything to make me fall, just as I said. Because this is about the 2028 elections,” Duterte added. — Bella Cariaso

articles.title: Prosecutors forgo plan to call Sara as witness
articles.summary: The prosecution team of the House of Representatives has decided to forego its plan to call Vice President Sara Duterte as a hostile witness at her impeachment trial, saying pressing her into taking…

blocks.text: October 13, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The prosecution team of the House of Representatives has decided to forego its plan to call Vice President Sara Duterte as a hostile witness at her impeachment trial, saying pressing her into taking the witness stand would only be an exercise in futility.

“We will no longer call the VP. From what we heard from the defense, what she is going to say is that she knows nothing – that’s all she is going to say in the witness stand,” private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan told reporters in a chance interview on the sidelines of the impeachment hearing yesterday.

“Then it’s not going to enlighten us, the senator-judges nor the public about her accountability for public funds, her accountability for unexplained wealth, her grave threats to the President, First Lady and (former) speaker and so on,” she explained.
“If that’s all she will say that she knows nothing, then it will only be useless,” Kapunan maintained.

“Just a warning to the defense: please, if you want to present the VP, please do so because I’m just dying to cross examine her. I will volunteer, I may not be the one (assigned to handle the case), but I certainly will volunteer,” she added.

But Kapunan emphasized that she and her colleagues in the prosecution would understand if the defense would be averse to letting her face the impeachment court as such would be risky and might even backfire.

“I think it would behoove the defense panel not to present the VP, because it would be good for the prosecution if they call the VP. Makikita natin ang init ng ulo niya, makikita natin ang pagka lutang niya (We will see her bad temper, her being dense),” she said.

She recalled that in the impeachment trial of the late chief justice Renato Corona in 2012, the latter blew his top during the hearing, prompting then Senate president and presiding officer Juan Ponce Enrile to put the entire Senate building on a lockdown to prevent a walkout.
“Remember the impeachment trial of CJ Corona? He was advised against taking the stand. He felt he was wronged and he showed it,” Kapunan said.
“I don’t think we are faltering,” Rep. Terry Ridon, one of the public prosecutors, said, denying insinuations that Duterte’s presence would complicate the prosecution’s position.
“We don’t need to call the VP. The documents are actually speaking for themselves. So, we don’t need a witness to speak on a document. We don’t need her as part of our evidence,” he said.
‘Revolving door’

At the resumption of Duterte’s impeachment trial yesterday, witness forensic accountant Alexander Cabrera testified that the flow of multimillion-peso managers’ checks and cash withdrawals in accounts of companies linked to the Vice President exhibits the behavior of typical money laundering operations.
Cabrera described a “revolving door” pattern in the movement of funds during an interjection by Sen. Risa Hontiveros.
“When money goes into a company and goes out the same day or the following day, it means it didn’t add any value to the company,” he said.
“That’s what happens in typical money laundering transactions,” he added.
The pattern is designed to obscure paper trail, he pointed out.
During the interjection, the specific accounts mentioned were those of GenCorp, Metro City Chow and Cale88 – all linked to the Vice President and her husband Manases Carpio.
Cabrera also pointed out the unusual nature of maintaining high-value time deposits without withdrawing the interest, but converting them into managers’ checks.
He noted that while Duterte did not sign the checks herself, her name was on the time deposits.
“To give up interest on a large amount like that doesn’t really make any business sense,” Cabrera said.

He also said that missing inventory, lack of standard receivables and payables and low utility footprints indicate that Cale88, described as local exporter of banana chips, may not be a functional manufacturing business.

Sen. Raffy Tulfo raised parallelism between traditional organized crime laundering techniques and the financial records of Cale88, saying illicit groups historically inject “dirty money” into legitimate front businesses to pay taxes and avoid tax evasion scrutiny.

When asked to analyze Cale88’s financial statements, Cabrera pointed out glaring discrepancies that deviate from standard industry operations. “Wala po siyang payable, wala po siyang receivable,” the witness testified.

Earlier during the trial, defense counsel Kristine Ferrer questioned Cabrera’s serving as prosecution witness, citing his membership in organizations that urged the Supreme Court to reconsider its ruling last year declaring the impeachment proceedings against Duterte unconstitutional.

The organizations wherein Cabrera is a member are the Management Association of the Philippines, Makati Business Club and the Justice Reform Initiative and Integrity Initiative. –Marc Jayson Cayabyab, Bella Cariaso

articles.title: Prosecution presents video of alleged suitcase deliveries to Romualdez at bail hearing
articles.summary: The prosecution in the plunder charges against former Speaker Martin Romualdez presented before the Sandiganbayan a video showing suitcases allegedly delivered to Romualdez's house in Forbes Park,…

blocks.text: Published October 12, 2026 11:57pm

The prosecution in the plunder charges against former Speaker Martin Romualdez presented before the Sandiganbayan a video showing suitcases allegedly delivered to Romualdez's house in Forbes Park, Makati City.
In a “24 Oras” report by Maki Pulido on Monday, a 13-second cellphone video was presented showing lined-up suitcases allegedly delivered to Romualdez on November 21, 2023.

The video was captured by George Villalon Jr., one of the so-called “Maleta Boys,” who is a former Marine and former bodyguard of fugitive ex-congressman Elizaldy Co. He was called to the witness stand to testify for the prosecution.

According to Villalon, the man in the black shirt seen in the video counting the suitcases was one of the former Speaker’s personnel. Meanwhile, he identified the man in the blue polo as John Paul Estrada, a former staff member of Co.
Villalon explained that he recorded the video of the suitcases, believed to be filled with cash, to send to his wife, who had missed-called him several times.

Screenshots of Villalon’s conversation with his wife were displayed on screen at the Sandiganbayan, showing that upon sending the video, he texted: “Puro pera laman niyan, deliver kay rumualdez (It’s all filled with money, delivered to rumualdez).”
His wife replied, “Akin na ang isa para magkapera man lang (Give me one so we can at least have some money).”
Villalon said he knew the suitcases contained cash after he assisted Estrada when a zipper on one of the suitcases broke.
Based on Villalon’s statement, he lost the cellphone he had used to record the video, but he was able to save the file on his laptop and copy it onto a flash drive to support Orly Guteza.

Guteza was also among the individuals who identified themselves as former bodyguards of Co. He previously testified before the Senate, but eventually retracted his statement, claiming he was merely coerced into accusing Romualdez on the orders of Senator Rodante Marcoleta and former senator Mike Defensor.

Aside from Villalon, Johnny Buduan also took the witness stand during the former Speaker’s first bail hearing. He is likewise a former Marine and former bodyguard of Co who was involved in the delivery of the suitcases.
Buduan said he knew the suitcases contained money because he helped Estrada transfer cash amounting to P30 million into a piece of luggage.
He further claimed that 14 of the suitcases were loaded into a Super Grandia Elite, while the rest were placed inside a black Innova.
In Pulido’s report, Buduan said that, based on a group chat of Co’s bodyguards, money deliveries to Romualdez’s house occurred two to three times a week.

During cross-examination, Romualdez’s lawyers pressed the witnesses into admitting that they did not personally or directly hand over the suitcases to the former Speaker, nor did they see him at the property where the delivery was made.

For his first bail hearing, the court permitted Romualdez to attend via videoconference. Present in person at the Sandiganbayan were at least eight of his defense lawyers. —Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Marcos: PH serious on nuclear energy amid future power demands of AI, data centers
articles.summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said that he is serious about his plans to establish nuclear power in the country in preparation for the anticipated high power demand of data and Artificial…

blocks.text: Published October 12, 2026 11:56pm

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said that he is serious about his plans to establish nuclear power in the country in preparation for the anticipated high power demand of data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) centers set to operate in the Philippines.

“We're serious about nuclear power because even as we stand now, we're okay in terms of power generation for the Philippines, but everybody knows that what's coming down the road is our data centers, is AI,” Marcos said.

“And I think everybody by now knows that the demand for power is going to increase at a very, very high rate, and if we are to be part and we want to be part of the value chain for AI, for the digital economy, we have to produce enough power to support it,” he added.
In July, Marcos announced that the US-led Pax Silica Industrial Hub for an AI supply chain is eyed to provide Filipinos with quality jobs. It is planned to be established in New Clark City in Tarlac.
However, the project received public criticism and concerns, especially for its anticipated daily power consumption of up to 3 gigawatts or 3 million kilowatts.

The President noted that nuclear energy is a viable option for the country, citing the reliability of power generators that do not heavily rely on oil, which has remained stable amid ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

“So yes, nuclear is one of the options that we have available to us that we are looking at very, very close to go along with... Because ang experience natin is very clear. It cannot be clearer,” Marcos said.

“Noong pumutok ang giyera sa Middle East at nagkagulo na ‘yung supply ng oil at saka presyo ng oil, ang hindi gumalaw yung 30% na production natin na galing sa local gas, hydro, solar, wind, biomass. Lahat ‘yan, hindi talaga gumalaw. And for a day or two, that's what we were depending on before we were able to secure supplies,” he added.

(When the war broke out in the Middle East and oil supply and prices went into turmoil, our 30% production from local gas, hydro, solar, wind, and biomass didn't fluctuate. All of those remained completely stable. And for a day or two, that's what we were depending on before we were able to secure supplies.)

On Saturday, the President expressed disappointment over the government’s decision to mothball the Bataan Nuclear Power Plant in the late 1980s, which was built during his late father’s administration.
Marcos made the remarks during his visit to the Singapore Nuclear Research and Safety Institute.
Work on the Bataan Nuclear Power Plant began in 1976 in response to rising energy prices. However, it never generated electricity after being mothballed following the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster.
In 2025, Marcos signed into law a bill creating an independent agency that will oversee the safe use of nuclear energy and radiation sources in the country. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: 2026 Trafficking Report: PH maintains Tier 1 ranking with POGO ban, conviction
articles.summary: The Philippines retained its Tier 1 ranking in the US State Department"s 2026 Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report, taking note of the government ban on offshore gaming operations and the conviction…

blocks.text: The Philippines retained its Tier 1 ranking in the US State Department’s 2026 Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report, taking note of the government ban on offshore gaming operations and the conviction of a former mayor in connection with a scam center.
"The government continued to demonstrate serious and sustained efforts during the reporting period; therefore, the Philippines remained on Tier 1," according to the Report.

"These efforts included enacting legislation banning offshore gaming operations and prescribing criminal liability for traffickers who recruit workers for such operations and convicting a former mayor accused of trafficking in connection with a scam center," it added.

The report also took note of other government efforts including, adopting a nationwide mandatory victim identification system and an enhanced NRM; increased the number of victims assisted; launch of a centralized interagency trafficking database; and expansion of the Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking’s (IACAT) prosecutorial task forces and prevention budget.
Trafficking in persons, human trafficking definition

According to the US Department of State website, “Trafficking in persons” and “human trafficking” are umbrella terms—often used interchangeably—to refer to a crime whereby traffickers exploit and profit at the expense of adults or children by compelling them to perform labor or engage in commercial sex. When a person younger than 18 is used to perform a commercial sex act, it is a crime regardless of whether there is any force, fraud, or coercion involved.

The United States recognizes two primary forms of trafficking in persons: sex trafficking and forced labor. The basic meaning of these forms of human trafficking, along with unique characteristics of each, are set forth below, followed by several key principles and concepts that relate to all forms of human trafficking.
Law enforcement efforts

The TIP report said that in 2025, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and the Philippine National Police (PNP) investigated 447 trafficking and OSAEC cases, compared with 500 cases in the previous reporting period.
The government prosecuted 366 alleged traffickers — 302 for sex trafficking and 64 for labor trafficking — compared with prosecuting 446 alleged traffickers in the previous reporting period.
The government continued 2,693 prosecutions initiated in prior years.
Courts convicted 103 traffickers — 91 for sex trafficking and 12 for labor trafficking — compared with 143 traffickers in the previous reporting period.
Of the 103 convicted, courts convicted 86 traffickers under the anti-trafficking law and 17 under related laws.

Courts sentenced convicted traffickers to penalties ranging from four years’ to life imprisonment and fines ranging from 30,000 to 10 million pesos ($510 to $169,750); the government sentenced the majority of convicted traffickers to at least one year of imprisonment.
Courts resolved 64 of 103 convictions through plea bargaining, reinforcing a victim-centered approach to minimize re-traumatization.
Meeting minimum standards
The Philippine government has met the minimum standards for eliminating human trafficking, the report said.

However, this year, fewer traffickers were convicted compared with the previous reporting period, there is a lack adequate digital forensics tools, personnel, and training to effectively investigate trafficking networks online, including in online sexual abuse or exploitation of children (OSAEC) and scam centers.

"The government did not report identifying any foreign national trafficking victims within scam centers, despite estimates that foreign nationals comprise 30 percent of scam centers’ workforce, and did not effectively detect, investigate, or address labor trafficking in the fishing industry," the report said.

"Due to inadequate and inconsistent screening throughout much of the reporting period, the government did not take effective measures to prevent the inappropriate penalization of potential victims solely for unlawful acts committed as a direct result of being trafficked. Corruption and official complicity in trafficking crimes remained significant concerns, inhibiting law enforcement action during the year."
Tier 1 for 11 consecutive years
The Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) welcomes the release of the report, adding that the country's Tier 1 ranking has been maintained for the 11th consecutive year.

“The DMW, as an active member of the Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (IACAT), considers this recognition a challenge to intensify further our efforts against illegal recruiters and human traffickers who exploit the vulnerabilities of our fellow Filipinos, particularly by strengthening protection for migrant workers and their families,” said Migrant Workers Secretary Hans Leo J. Cacdac in a statement.

The DMW, in partnership with the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA), helped repatriate at least 1,606 identified victims of illegal recruitment and trafficking, many of whom were rescued from forced labor in scam compounds in Myanmar, Cambodia, and Laos.
The agency added that returning survivors received comprehensive DMW AKSYON Fund assistance, including medical care, psychosocial support, legal aid, financial assistance, and emergency shelter.

The department identified critical areas that require stronger action, such as reversing the decline in trafficking convictions, building digital-forensics capacity to combat online syndicates, screening foreign victims in scam compounds, and bolstering protections for Filipino seafarers and commercial fishers vulnerable to labor trafficking.

“The DMW will translate these findings into intensified monitoring of deceptive online recruitment, strengthened evidence gathering for criminal prosecutions, and strict adherence to the non-punishment principle for victims. It will also expand nationwide information drives, including across social media, to help overseas Filipino workers recognize recruitment scams and report suspected traffickers,” Cacdac noted. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Cyber-attack defrosts refrigerators in two French supermarket chains
articles.summary:
An estimated 150-200 Intermarché shops were targeted, along with almost 100 Cooperative U outlets

French supermarket chains Intermarché and Cooperative U have been hit by an “unprecedented”…

blocks.text: French supermarket chains Intermarché and Cooperative U have been hit by an “unprecedented” cyber-attack that caused their refrigerators to defrost, the two retailers have said.
An estimated 150-200 Intermarché shops were targeted, along with almost 100 Cooperative U outlets, in the attack, they said on Monday.
Paris prosecutors confirmed the attack, which reportedly also hit other major chains, and said it had prompted outbreaks of fire.

According to BFM TV, France’s largest supermarket chain E. Leclerc was also affected, with hackers “managing to remotely trigger the forced defrosting of the refrigeration systems in numerous stores”. E. Leclerc did not immediately confirm the information.
Those branches that were affected would have to “throw away all of the products” that are fresh and frozen, Intermarché said.
The chief executive of Cooperative U, Dominique Schelcher, described the attack as “unprecedented” and confirmed it had affected refrigeration systems since Sunday night.
“Targeting equipment essential to the preservation of fresh products and to the food supply of the French people is extremely serious and is unprecedented. It is unacceptable,” he wrote on X.
He added that the company’s teams are “fully mobilised” to restore the situation as quickly as possible.
“An investigation will be necessary to shed full light on this attack,” he added.

The office of the Paris prosecutor confirmed to AFP that an investigation has been opened into “the large-scale cyber-attack affecting the refrigerators of several major food retail chains across France”.
The probe will help “identify the victims and establish the link with the damage they reported in terms of foodstuff losses and the outbreak of fires”, the prosecutor’s office said.
after newsletter promotion

Intermarché condemned the food waste and financial losses resulting from the attack, without providing figures, and warned there could be issues with insurance policies which do not “cover this type” of in-store incident.
BFM TV said temperatures were “altered remotely, resulting in the destruction of stocks of fresh and frozen products”.
The incident comes against the background of growing concern over the potential havoc that can be caused in Europe in all sectors by cyber-attacks by malicious actors.

President Emmanuel Macron, a strong supporter of Ukraine in its fight against the Russian invasion, last month ordered measures to protect France’s critical infrastructure from Russian “hybrid attacks”.

articles.title: Villanueva questions Cale88 stock sale to firm with sari-sari store assets
articles.summary: Senator-judge Joel Villanueva said Monday that the stocks of Cale88 Foods Corporation, a declared asset of Vice President Sara Duterte"s husband, Manases Carpio, were sold in 2025 to a certain firm…

blocks.text: Published October 12, 2026 11:15pm

Senator-judge Joel Villanueva said Monday that the stocks of Cale88 Foods Corporation, a declared asset of Vice President Sara Duterte’s husband, Manases Carpio, were sold in 2025 to a certain firm that had only P84,000 worth of assets.

Villanueva made the observation after prosecution witness and lawyer Alex Cabrera, also a certified public accountant, testified that stocks of Calle 88 Foods Corporation were bought out by Pikimong Pikimong, an entity which has only around P84,000 in assets and even lower capital based on its corporate records.
Villanueva said that such an amount of assets is lower than Cale88's P150 million reported sales in 2024. It also had no listed rank-and-file employees based on its corporate filings.

“Pikimong Pikimong had only about P59,836 pesos in capital and approximately P84,700 in total assets, with no corresponding acquisition reflected in its financial statements. So parang sinasabi niyo po, 'yung sari-sari store, binili ‘yung isang department store?,” Villanueva said during Day 38 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Duterte.
Cabrera replied, ‘Yung dilis po, kinain iyong pating.”
(The tiny fish ate a shark.)

Cabrera earlier testified that the Duterte-Carpio couple has an unexplained wealth of P817 million based on forensic investigation of their financial records, including bank and corporate records. This P817 million includes those undeclared assets stemming from their shares in their business interests, including Cale88.
Villanueva then asked the witness if he saw proof that there was a genuine sale of Pikimong Pikimong buying stocks from Cale88 aside from the General Information Sheet of the two firms.
Cabrera answered none, adding that a GIS entry does not prove a sale indeed happened.

“Wala po [na proof of sale]. You could have seen the deed of sale, check payment, a cheque being cleared being reflected in the bank account, recording of the sale in the books, the journal entry stating a sale. The stock and transfer books should likewise reflect it,” he said.
“We need a menu of all the transaction documents that will be affected and will reflect the record of the transaction. That is the normal process,” he added.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: US federal agents search home of Trump critic Ilhan Omar
articles.summary: Justice Department officials said the Washington residence of Democratic Congresswoman Ilhan Omar, an outspoken opponent of President Trump, was raided as "part of an ongoing federal investigation."

image.caption: The US Justice Department did not share details of their investigationImage: Annabelle Gordon/REUTERS

blocks.text: US federal agents searched the home of a Democratic congresswoman and outspoken critic of President Donald Trump on Monday, the Department of Justice (DoJ) confirmed.
Officials from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the investigative arm of US immigration enforcement, were seen early on Monday morning outside the Washington home of Ilhan Omar.

"Today in the Washington, DC area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice," a DoJ spokesperson told the Reuters news agency in a statement which didn't specifically name Omar.
"This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal investigation."
Who is Ilhan Omar?

Omar, who came to the United States from Somalia as a child, was first elected to Congress in 2018 and is a member of the group of left-wing Democratic lawmakers known as "The Squad," who have been among Trump's most vocal opponents.
Omar represents a district including Minneapolis, home to one of the largest Somali communities in the US – a community which Trump has frequently targeted in racist outbursts.

blocks.caption: Omar has said Trump has a 'creepy obsession' with her Image: Mark Schiefelbein/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: He ​previously called Somalis "garbage" and said in February that Omar and Democratic Representative Rashida Tlaib of Michigan should be "institutionalized" and sent back to "where they came from."

Last ​week, Trump called Democratic candidate for US Senate from Michigan Abdul El Sayed a "RADICAL Extremist" and "Terrorist Sympathizer" while offering support for the Republican candidate, Mike Rogers
Democrats decry 'abuse of power'
House Democratic leaders condemned the search as an "abuse of power" by the Trump administration.
Omar said she will “not be silenced” and called the search of her home the “latest escalation” in President Donald Trump’s '‘intimidation" campaign.

blocks.caption: Trump has been accused of weaponizing US agenices to go after his political opponentsImage: J. Scott Applewhite/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Omar has called Trump's focus on her an "unhealthy and creepy obsession" said she and her family have faced death threats, which she attributes ⁠to "hateful political rhetoric" especially ​from Trump.
On Monday, Omar said she will "not be silenced" and called the search of her home the "latest escalation" in Trump's "intimidation" campaign.

No charges against Omar were announced in connection with Monday's search, but US media reported that the operation was linked to a criminal fraud investigation into immigration paperwork submitted on her behalf by her late father when she was a child.
The search comes just three weeks before midterm elections in which Trump's Republicans will be trying to defend their thin majorities in the US.
